mapping.pmtools_method: Inputs: a specimen-frame vector (x, y, z) in Am2 (PMD/CSV: file values; SQUID/RS3: rebuilt from Dcore/Icore and mag*volume, then x,y,z rounded to 3 significant digits only for display/storage, parserSQUID.ts:94) and the header a (core azimuth, degrees), b, s (bedding strike, degrees), d (bedding dip, degrees). Preprocessing of b: the file value is a hade (angle from vertical down); the store holds the plunge b_app = 90 - b_file (parsedData.ts:45; SQUID/RS3 parsers do the same locally, parserSQUID.ts:86, parserRS3.ts:71). Step 1 (geographic): v_geo = M(a, b_app) . v with M = [[cos a sin p, -sin a, cos p cos a],[sin a sin p, cos a, sin a cos p],[-cos p, 0, sin p]], p = b_app in radians (matrix.ts:18-22). Columns are the geographic directions of the specimen axes: X -> (a, b_app - 90) = (a, -hade), Y -> (a + 90, 0), Z -> (a, b_app) = core axis with azimuth a and plunge 90 - hade. Step 2 (stratigraphic): dipDirection = s + 90 (right-hand rule, dip to the right of strike); v_strat = Rz(dd) . Ry(d) . Rz(-dd) . v_geo, where Rz(theta) = rotateTo(theta, 90) adds theta to the declination and Ry(d) = rotateTo(0, 90 - d) = [[cos d, 0, sin d],[0,1,0],[-sin d, 0, cos d]] rotates about the strike axis by d so that the bedding pole (dd+180, 90-d) goes to vertical (Coordinates.ts:160-168). Overturned beds are expressed as d > 90 and rotate by the full angle; no flag, no flip. Output: dec = atan2(y, x) in degrees plus 360 if negative (no modulo, so exactly 360.0 can occur), inc = asin(z/|v|); length preserved (Coordinates.ts:39-52). Displayed values are rounded with toFixed(1) (tooltips, interpretation table, MetaDataChange). No polarity flip, no normalisation, no iteration, no randomness; angles in degrees throughout, declination clockwise from north, inclination positive down. The 'specimen' reference returns the vector unchanged.

mapping.verdict_explanation: PMTools' live specimen -> geographic -> stratigraphic transform is the same rotation as pmag.dogeo followed by pmag.dotilt once the orientation inputs are mapped: az = a, pl = b_stored - 90 (= -hade as written in the file), bed_az = s + 90, bed_dip = d. This adapter is not a choice of mine: it is exactly what PmagPy's own PMD importer writes (convert_2_magic.py:9319-9326) and what pmag.orient or_con 1 produces (pmag.py:1095-1096). Over 5590 synthetic cases (random plus the full edge grid of declination wrap, inclination +-90, vertical/horizontal cores, vertical/overturned beds) the largest difference is 3.3e-11 degrees in declination and 7.1e-15 in unit-vector components; on real PMD and SQUID files it is 1e-13 degrees. The only caveats are comparison conventions (both sides can emit 360.0; declination undefined at |inc| = 90) and the fact that PMTools keeps the vector length while PmagPy normalises, which does not affect dec/inc. Nothing is random.

adapters_required: Core dip: file b is a hade; PMTools stores plunge b = 90 - b_file (parsedData.ts:45). PmagPy pl = -b_file = b_stored - 90. Do not pass the stored b to dogeo directly.

Core azimuth: az = a unchanged for PMD/CSV/XLSX. For SQUID use the parser's a (a_file - 90 mod 360, parserSQUID.ts:37; = pmag.orient or_con 2). For RS3 use the parser's a (unchanged) and its P1/P3-adjusted b (not verified).

Bedding: PMD/CSV/XLSX s is a strike with dip to the right; bed_az = s + 90 (identical to convert_2_magic.py:9324). For RS3 the file BDec is a dip direction and the parser stores s = BDec - 90 (parserRS3.ts:34), so bed_az = s_parser + 90 = BDec.
Bedding dip d unchanged; overturned beds as d > 90 on both sides, no flag.
Specimen direction: (dec, inc) = pmag.cart2dir([x, y, z]) from PMTools' step x,y,z (for SQUID/RS3 oracles prefer the file's Dcore/Icore to avoid the 3-significant-digit rounding of stored x,y,z).

Output comparison: declination modulo 360 (both sides can return 360.0: Coordinates.ts:47-49 adds 2 pi without a modulo; cart2dir's % 360 rounds to 360.0 for tiny negative residues); at |inc| = 90 declination is undefined, compare unit vectors instead; PMTools length is |xyz|, PmagPy is 1.
Rounded display values: apply round-half-up toFixed(1) semantics on top of the oracle chain or test the unrounded value.
convention_differences: Core dip sign/kind: PMD b = hade from vertical; PMTools stores plunge 90 - b (shown and edited as 'Core Dip' plunge); PmagPy 'dip' = plunge of the lab arrow = -b (negative). Same physics (specimen X -> (a, -hade), Y -> (a+90, 0), Z -> (a, 90-hade) on both sides, verified numerically).

Bedding azimuth: PMTools takes a strike (correctBedding adds 90 itself); PmagPy takes the dip direction (bed_az). Strike + 90 = dip direction under the right-hand rule used by both PMTools and convert_2_magic.pmd.
Declination range: PMTools [0, 360] inclusive (360.0 possible), PmagPy [0, 360] with 360.0 possible after float rounding; 515 vs 416 of the 5590 cases emitted 360.0 - compare modulo 360.
Vector length: PMTools preserves it; PmagPy returns unit vectors (R is dropped).

Thesis vs code naming: thesis.txt:196-197 says the specimen X axis 'coincides with the dip line' and Y with the 'right strike line'; code maps X to the up-dip direction (inc = -hade) and Y to a + 90, consistent with that qualitative description; the code comments cite Tauxe 9.3 / A3.12 (toReferenceCoordinates.ts:26, matrix.ts:15), not the thesis, and matrix.ts:15-16 notes it uses the core dip directly instead of Tauxe's lab-arrow plunge (x - 90).

mapping.thesis_agreement: The thesis gives no rotation formula; it only defines the three frames (thesis.txt:193-206): specimen (X 'coincides with the dip line', Y with the 'right strike line', Z down), geographic ('marking plane coincides with the current horizontal plane'), stratigraphic ('marking plane coincides with the primary horizontal plane of the rock'), and names the CORE/GEO/STRAT menu (thesis.txt:855-857) and the Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat interpretation table (thesis.txt:942-946). The code is consistent with that qualitative description: with a = core azimuth and stored b = plunge (90 - hade), the specimen X axis maps to (a, -hade) (the up-dip line of the marking plane), Y to (a + 90, 0) (the right-hand strike line) and Z to (a, 90 - hade) (the core axis) - verified numerically from the matrix columns and identical to pmag.dogeo. The implementation comments cite Tauxe (toReferenceCoordinates.ts:26 '9.3 Changing coordinate systems', matrix.ts:15 'A3.12') rather than the thesis. The published paper text (FZE0150.txt) has no coordinate-transform passage (grep empty). Nothing in the thesis contradicts the code; the thesis simply does not specify the method, so the thesis cannot serve as a numerical reference for this row and PmagPy is the only oracle.
mapping.confidence_reason: Every claim rests on opened source lines (PMTools and PmagPy 4.3.14, version printed as pmagpy-4.3.14) or on commands run in this session; the oracle agreement was measured on 5590 synthetic cases spanning every edge the row calls for plus real PMD and SQUID files, with the adapter independently corroborated by PmagPy's own PMD importer, pmag.orient or_con 1/2 and the lab software's columns inside 406c.squid. The one thing not verified is the Agico P1-P4 semantics behind the RS3 parser branch, which I have isolated as a parser-level open question rather than part of this row's verdict. final.pmtools_method: Inputs: a specimen-frame vector (x, y, z) in Am2 (PMD/CSV: file values; SQUID/RS3: rebuilt from Dcore/Icore and mag*volume, then x,y,z rounded to 3 significant digits only for display/storage, parserSQUID.ts:94) and the header a (core azimuth, degrees), b, s (bedding strike, degrees), d (bedding dip, degrees). Preprocessing of b: the file value is a hade (angle from vertical down); the store holds the plunge b_app = 90 - b_file (parsedData.ts:45; SQUID/RS3 parsers do the same locally, parserSQUID.ts:86, parserRS3.ts:71). Step 1 (geographic): v_geo = M(a, b_app) . v with M = [[cos a sin p, -sin a, cos p cos a],[sin a sin p, cos a, sin a cos p],[-cos p, 0, sin p]], p = b_app in radians (matrix.ts:18-22). Columns are the geographic directions of the specimen axes: X -> (a, b_app - 90) = (a, -hade), Y -> (a + 90, 0), Z -> (a, b_app) = core axis with azimuth a and plunge 90 - hade. Step 2 (stratigraphic): dipDirection = s + 90 (right-hand rule, dip to the right of strike); v_strat = Rz(dd) . Ry(d) . Rz(-dd) . v_geo, where Rz(theta) = rotateTo(theta, 90) adds theta to the declination and Ry(d) = rotateTo(0, 90 - d) = [[cos d, 0, sin d],[0,1,0],[-sin d, 0, cos d]] rotates about the strike axis by d so that the bedding pole (dd+180, 90-d) goes to vertical (Coordinates.ts:160-168). Overturned beds are expressed as d > 90 and rotate by the full angle; no flag, no flip. Output: dec = atan2(y, x) in degrees plus 360 if negative (no modulo, so exactly 360.0 can occur), inc = asin(z/|v|); length preserved (Coordinates.ts:39-52). Displayed values are rounded with toFixed(1) (tooltips, interpretation table, MetaDataChange). No polarity flip, no normalisation, no iteration, no randomness; angles in degrees throughout, declination clockwise from north, inclination positive down. The 'specimen' reference returns the vector unchanged.

final.verdict_explanation: PMTools' live specimen -> geographic -> stratigraphic transform is the same rotation as pmag.dogeo followed by pmag.dotilt once the orientation inputs are mapped: az = a, pl = b_stored - 90 (= -hade as written in the file), bed_az = s + 90, bed_dip = d. This adapter is not a choice of mine: it is exactly what PmagPy's own PMD importer writes (convert_2_magic.py:9319-9326) and what pmag.orient or_con 1 produces (pmag.py:1095-1096). Over 5590 synthetic cases (random plus the full edge grid of declination wrap, inclination +-90, vertical/horizontal cores, vertical/overturned beds) the largest difference is 3.3e-11 degrees in declination and 7.1e-15 in unit-vector components; on real PMD and SQUID files it is 1e-13 degrees. The only caveats are comparison conventions (both sides can emit 360.0; declination undefined at |inc| = 90) and the fact that PMTools keeps the vector length while PmagPy normalises, which does not affect dec/inc. Nothing is random.

adapters_required: Core dip: file b is a hade; PMTools stores plunge b = 90 - b_file (parsedData.ts:45). PmagPy pl = -b_file = b_stored - 90. Do not pass the stored b to dogeo directly.

Core azimuth: az = a unchanged for PMD/CSV/XLSX. For SQUID use the parser's a (a_file - 90 mod 360, parserSQUID.ts:37; = pmag.orient or_con 2). For RS3 use the parser's a (unchanged) and its P1/P3-adjusted b (not verified).

Bedding: PMD/CSV/XLSX s is a strike with dip to the right; bed_az = s + 90 (identical to convert_2_magic.py:9324). For RS3 the file BDec is a dip direction and the parser stores s = BDec - 90 (parserRS3.ts:34), so bed_az = s_parser + 90 = BDec.
Bedding dip d unchanged; overturned beds as d > 90 on both sides, no flag.
Specimen direction: (dec, inc) = pmag.cart2dir([x, y, z]) from PMTools' step x,y,z (for SQUID/RS3 oracles prefer the file's Dcore/Icore to avoid the 3-significant-digit rounding of stored x,y,z).

Output comparison: declination modulo 360 (both sides can return 360.0: Coordinates.ts:47-49 adds 2 pi without a modulo; cart2dir's % 360 rounds to 360.0 for tiny negative residues); at |inc| = 90 declination is undefined, compare unit vectors instead; PMTools length is |xyz|, PmagPy is 1.
Rounded display values: apply round-half-up toFixed(1) semantics on top of the oracle chain or test the unrounded value.
convention_differences: Core dip sign/kind: PMD b = hade from vertical; PMTools stores plunge 90 - b (shown and edited as 'Core Dip' plunge); PmagPy 'dip' = plunge of the lab arrow = -b (negative). Same physics (specimen X -> (a, -hade), Y -> (a+90, 0), Z -> (a, 90-hade) on both sides, verified numerically).

Bedding azimuth: PMTools takes a strike (correctBedding adds 90 itself); PmagPy takes the dip direction (bed_az). Strike + 90 = dip direction under the right-hand rule used by both PMTools and convert_2_magic.pmd.
Declination range: PMTools [0, 360] inclusive (360.0 possible), PmagPy [0, 360] with 360.0 possible after float rounding; 515 vs 416 of the 5590 cases emitted 360.0 - compare modulo 360.
Vector length: PMTools preserves it; PmagPy returns unit vectors (R is dropped).

Thesis vs code naming: thesis.txt:196-197 says the specimen X axis 'coincides with the dip line' and Y with the 'right strike line'; code maps X to the up-dip direction (inc = -hade) and Y to a + 90, consistent with that qualitative description; the code comments cite Tauxe 9.3 / A3.12 (toReferenceCoordinates.ts:26, matrix.ts:15), not the thesis, and matrix.ts:15-16 notes it uses the core dip directly instead of Tauxe's lab-arrow plunge (x - 90).

final.thesis_agreement: The thesis gives no rotation formula; it only defines the three frames (thesis.txt:193-206): specimen (X 'coincides with the dip line', Y with the 'right strike line', Z down), geographic ('marking plane coincides with the current horizontal plane'), stratigraphic ('marking plane coincides with the primary horizontal plane of the rock'), and names the CORE/GEO/STRAT menu (thesis.txt:855-857) and the Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat interpretation table (thesis.txt:942-946). The code is consistent with that qualitative description: with a = core azimuth and stored b = plunge (90 - hade), the specimen X axis maps to (a, -hade) (the up-dip line of the marking plane), Y to (a + 90, 0) (the right-hand strike line) and Z to (a, 90 - hade) (the core axis) - verified numerically from the matrix columns and identical to pmag.dogeo. The implementation comments cite Tauxe (toReferenceCoordinates.ts:26 '9.3 Changing coordinate systems', matrix.ts:15 'A3.12') rather than the thesis. The published paper text (FZE0150.txt) has no coordinate-transform passage (grep empty). Nothing in the thesis contradicts the code; the thesis simply does not specify the method, so the thesis cannot serve as a numerical reference for this row and PmagPy is the only oracle.
final.confidence_reason: Every claim rests on opened source lines (PMTools and PmagPy 4.3.14, version printed as pmagpy-4.3.14) or on commands run in this session; the oracle agreement was measured on 5590 synthetic cases spanning every edge the row calls for plus real PMD and SQUID files, with the adapter independently corroborated by PmagPy's own PMD importer, pmag.orient or_con 1/2 and the lab software's columns inside 406c.squid. The one thing not verified is the Agico P1-P4 semantics behind the RS3 parser branch, which I have isolated as a parser-level open question rather than part of this row's verdict. mapping.pmtools_method: fisherMean(directions) (calculateFisherMean.ts:21-94): each Direction(dec, inc, length) is converted to Cartesian x=L cos D cos I, y=L sin D cos I, z=L sin I (Direction.ts:33-35; every caller passes L=1, so unit vectors); Xbar = component-wise sum; R = |Xbar|; mean direction = Xbar/R via atan2/asin with dec mapped to [0,360) by adding 2pi when negative (Coordinates.ts:43-51). k = (N-1)/(N-R) and csd = 81/sqrt(k) when N != R, else k = Infinity, csd = 0 (lines 60-66). a95: b = 20^(1/(N-1)) - 1; a = 1 - b*(N-R)/R; if a < -1 then a = -1; a95 = acos(a) in degrees; if a < 0 then a95 = 180 (lines 68-72). Result keys: direction (Direction), MAD (holds a95), k, N, R, csd (lines 74-81). Units: degrees in and out; dec in [0,360), inc in [-90,90]. Constants: 20 = 1/p with p = 0.05; 81 for csd. No iteration, no randomness. Edge behaviour (verified by run): N=1 -> b = Infinity, a = NaN, a95 = NaN, k = Infinity, csd = 0, R = 1; identical directions or all-vertical (R == N exactly) -> k = Infinity, a95 = 0, csd = 0; antipodal pair (R ~ 1e-16) -> a95 = 180, k = 0.5, dec/inc are numerical noise; N=0 (possible only via the VGP path with an empty list) -> NaN direction. Live DIR path preprocessing (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:17-38): rows selected by 1-based index; rows whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs are flipped with reversePolarity() (inc = -inc, dec = (dec+180) % 360, JS % keeps the sign of a negative dec); then every Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat is rounded with toFixed(1) (round-half-away-from-zero on the exact binary value) BEFORE the mean; the wrapper (calculateFisherMean.ts:5-19) computes the geographic and stratigraphic means from the same rows. Displayed values are then rounded again to 0.1 (formatter lines 35-42 and table valueFormatters). The VGP pole-mean path feeds Direction(poleLongitude, poleLatitude, 1) with no rounding of the poles (Graphs.tsx:26-30), although the site directions upstream are rounded to 0.1 before the VGP calculation (VGPmodalContent.tsx:69-74).

mapping.verdict_explanation: fisherMean is a literal port of pmag.fisher_mean (same unit-vector sum, same R, same k = (N-1)/(N-R), same csd = 81/sqrt(k), same a95 with the a < -1 clamp and the a < 0 -> 180 rule). On 20 identical-input cases (real sample.dir through the live DIR path with polarity flips, the six-direction fixture, N=2, identical, antipodal, vertical, near-vertical, declination wrap, poles, the PmagPy docstring example) every numeric output agrees to <= 5.7e-14 (one ULP at the 360-degree scale, caused only by atan2+2pi vs % 360). The adapter has to (1) emulate the live DIR preprocessing (flip the user-marked rows, then round every value to 0.1 with Decimal(x).quantize(Decimal('0.1'), ROUND_HALF_UP), which I verified reproduces JS toFixed(1) on all 14 tie probes where Python round() and Decimal(str(x)) both fail), (2) map PmagPy's string 'inf' to Infinity, (3) skip k/a95/n/r/csd when N < 2 because PmagPy returns only dec/inc there, and (4) rename keys (MAD -> alpha95, N -> n, R -> r). No numerical mismatch exists; the only differences are representational (N=1 NaN/Infinity vs no statistics; Infinity vs 'inf'; the field and column name 'MAD' for a95, already catalogued as locked and harmless).

adapters_required: Input shape: PMTools IDirData rows -> two lists of [dec, inc] pairs ([Dgeo, Igeo] and [Dstrat, Istrat]); call pmag.fisher_mean once per frame (PMTools' wrapper returns both frames from one call).

Live DIR path preprocessing (only when testing through calculateStatisticsDIR): for each row whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs set inc = -inc and dec = math.fmod(dec + 180, 360) (JS % keeps the sign; use fmod not % so a negative dec behaves the same), then round every Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat with float(Decimal(x).quantize(Decimal('0.1'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)). Verified: this matches JS toFixed(1) on 14 tie probes; Python round() differs on 10.25, -10.25, 0.25, -0.25, -33.25; Decimal(str(x)) differs on 1.15, 359.95, 0.35, -0.35, 45.05, 45.15.
Selection: PMTools selects rows by 1-based index in selectedDirectionsIDs (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:18) but flips by row id (line 23); the adapter must apply the same two keys.
k representation: map PmagPy 'inf' (string) to Infinity, or compare 1/k (0 on both sides).
N < 2: compare only dec/inc; PmagPy has no n/r/k/csd/alpha95 there, PMTools has a95 NaN and k Infinity.
Key renames: direction.declination->dec, direction.inclination->inc, MAD->alpha95, k->k, N->n, R->r, csd->csd.
Degenerate R ~ 0 (antipodal sets): do not compare dec/inc (noise on both sides); a95 (180), k and csd remain comparable.
Pole mean (PB-05 reuse): Direction(poleLongitude, poleLatitude, 1) -> [lon, lat] pairs with no rounding (Graphs.tsx:26-30); the same k/'inf' and N<2 rules apply.
convention_differences: Declination normalisation: PMTools adds 2pi when atan2 < 0 (Coordinates.ts:47-49); PmagPy uses (arctan2/rad) % 360 (pmag.py:2615). Same range [0, 360), last-ULP differences only.
k when R == N: PMTools number Infinity (calculateFisherMean.ts:64); PmagPy string 'inf' (pmag.py:4489).
N < 2: PmagPy returns {'dec','inc'} only (pmag.py:4465-4467); PMTools computes a95 = NaN (20^(1/0) - 1 = Infinity, times (N-R) = 0 gives NaN) and k = Infinity.

Field naming: PMTools stores a95 under MeanDir.MAD (GlobalTypes.ts:167-174), shows it under the table header MADgeo/MADstrat and under the tooltip key 'MAD' on the DIR page, but under 'a95' on the VGP page; PmagPy calls it alpha95.
Live DIR preprocessing (polarity flip of user-marked rows, rounding of inputs to 0.1 deg) has no counterpart inside pmag.fisher_mean; fisher_by_pol flips automatically instead of by user choice.
Frames: one PMTools call returns geographic and stratigraphic means; PmagPy is one frame per call.
Intensity: PMTools Direction carries a length but every caller passes 1; PmagPy discards the third column (pmag.py:4471). Equivalent for all live callers.

Modulo of a negative declination after the flip: JS (-200 + 180) % 360 = -20, Python % gives 340 (math.fmod gives -20). Only matters if a CSV/XLSX/MDIR parser yields a negative declination; .dir files cannot (fixed-width, parserDIR.ts:29-38).

mapping.thesis_agreement: Matches. thesis.txt:348-363 (section 1.3) gives formula (1.4) k = (N-1)/(N-R) and formula (1.5) alpha(1-p) = arccos(1 - (N-R)/R * ((1/p)^(1/(N-1)) - 1)) with p = 0.05, i.e. 1/p = 20; calculateFisherMean.ts:61 and 68-71 implement exactly these with the constant 20 (and pmag.py:4486, 4492-4494 likewise). The thesis does not describe csd = 81/sqrt(k), the a < -1 clamp, the a < 0 -> 180 rule, the 0.1-degree input rounding or the user polarity flip; those come from the PmagPy port (comment at calculateFisherMean.ts:38) and from calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:23-30. UI chapter: thesis.txt:1009-1012 lists the FISHER method button; thesis.txt:1049-1052 says the results table shows 'MAD or a95 and k' (so the shared MAD column for a95 is by design); thesis.txt:1074-1078 says the VGP stereogram automatically shows the Fisher mean, matching Graphs.tsx:25-42 and dataToStereoVGP.ts:55-85.
mapping.confidence_reason: Every claim rests on opened source lines (PMTools and pmag.py/ipmag.py 4.3.14) and on 20 identical-input runs plus two targeted probes (rounding-tie emulation on 14 values; R == N behaviour on 30 identical-direction sets), all reproduced from scripts kept in the scratchpad (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-i1948374-PMTools/bdb3b478-28ac-4114-92f5-3720a2d0303d/scratchpad/PB-02-map/oracle.py, compare.py, py_round.py, py_rn.py, pmtools_results.json, pmagpy_results.json). The PMTools function is a literal port of pmag.fisher_mean and the observed maximum difference outside degenerate inputs is 5.7e-14. Not verified: behaviour of the CSV/XLSX/MDIR DIR parsers for negative or multi-decimal declinations (only relevant to the fmod and rounding adapter notes), and the VGP cache contents beyond the rounding lines cited (PB-05's scope).

final.pmtools_method: fisherMean(directions) (calculateFisherMean.ts:21-94): each Direction(dec, inc, length) is converted to Cartesian x=L cos D cos I, y=L sin D cos I, z=L sin I (Direction.ts:33-35; every caller passes L=1, so unit vectors); Xbar = component-wise sum; R = |Xbar|; mean direction = Xbar/R via atan2/asin with dec mapped to [0,360) by adding 2pi when negative (Coordinates.ts:43-51). k = (N-1)/(N-R) and csd = 81/sqrt(k) when N != R, else k = Infinity, csd = 0 (lines 60-66). a95: b = 20^(1/(N-1)) - 1; a = 1 - b*(N-R)/R; if a < -1 then a = -1; a95 = acos(a) in degrees; if a < 0 then a95 = 180 (lines 68-72). Result keys: direction (Direction), MAD (holds a95), k, N, R, csd (lines 74-81). Units: degrees in and out; dec in [0,360), inc in [-90,90]. Constants: 20 = 1/p with p = 0.05; 81 for csd. No iteration, no randomness. Edge behaviour (verified by run): N=1 -> b = Infinity, a = NaN, a95 = NaN, k = Infinity, csd = 0, R = 1; identical directions or all-vertical (R == N exactly) -> k = Infinity, a95 = 0, csd = 0; antipodal pair (R ~ 1e-16) -> a95 = 180, k = 0.5, dec/inc are numerical noise; N=0 (possible only via the VGP path with an empty list) -> NaN direction. Live DIR path preprocessing (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:17-38): rows selected by 1-based index; rows whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs are flipped with reversePolarity() (inc = -inc, dec = (dec+180) % 360, JS % keeps the sign of a negative dec); then every Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat is rounded with toFixed(1) (round-half-away-from-zero on the exact binary value) BEFORE the mean; the wrapper (calculateFisherMean.ts:5-19) computes the geographic and stratigraphic means from the same rows. Displayed values are then rounded again to 0.1 (formatter lines 35-42 and table valueFormatters). The VGP pole-mean path feeds Direction(poleLongitude, poleLatitude, 1) with no rounding of the poles (Graphs.tsx:26-30), although the site directions upstream are rounded to 0.1 before the VGP calculation (VGPmodalContent.tsx:69-74).

final.verdict_explanation: fisherMean is a literal port of pmag.fisher_mean (same unit-vector sum, same R, same k = (N-1)/(N-R), same csd = 81/sqrt(k), same a95 with the a < -1 clamp and the a < 0 -> 180 rule). On 20 identical-input cases (real sample.dir through the live DIR path with polarity flips, the six-direction fixture, N=2, identical, antipodal, vertical, near-vertical, declination wrap, poles, the PmagPy docstring example) every numeric output agrees to <= 5.7e-14 (one ULP at the 360-degree scale, caused only by atan2+2pi vs % 360). The adapter has to (1) emulate the live DIR preprocessing (flip the user-marked rows, then round every value to 0.1 with Decimal(x).quantize(Decimal('0.1'), ROUND_HALF_UP), which I verified reproduces JS toFixed(1) on all 14 tie probes where Python round() and Decimal(str(x)) both fail), (2) map PmagPy's string 'inf' to Infinity, (3) skip k/a95/n/r/csd when N < 2 because PmagPy returns only dec/inc there, and (4) rename keys (MAD -> alpha95, N -> n, R -> r). No numerical mismatch exists; the only differences are representational (N=1 NaN/Infinity vs no statistics; Infinity vs 'inf'; the field and column name 'MAD' for a95, already catalogued as locked and harmless).

adapters_required: Input shape: PMTools IDirData rows -> two lists of [dec, inc] pairs ([Dgeo, Igeo] and [Dstrat, Istrat]); call pmag.fisher_mean once per frame (PMTools' wrapper returns both frames from one call).

Live DIR path preprocessing (only when testing through calculateStatisticsDIR): for each row whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs set inc = -inc and dec = math.fmod(dec + 180, 360) (JS % keeps the sign; use fmod not % so a negative dec behaves the same), then round every Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat with float(Decimal(x).quantize(Decimal('0.1'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)). Verified: this matches JS toFixed(1) on 14 tie probes; Python round() differs on 10.25, -10.25, 0.25, -0.25, -33.25; Decimal(str(x)) differs on 1.15, 359.95, 0.35, -0.35, 45.05, 45.15.
Selection: PMTools selects rows by 1-based index in selectedDirectionsIDs (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:18) but flips by row id (line 23); the adapter must apply the same two keys.
k representation: map PmagPy 'inf' (string) to Infinity, or compare 1/k (0 on both sides).
N < 2: compare only dec/inc; PmagPy has no n/r/k/csd/alpha95 there, PMTools has a95 NaN and k Infinity.
Key renames: direction.declination->dec, direction.inclination->inc, MAD->alpha95, k->k, N->n, R->r, csd->csd.
Degenerate R ~ 0 (antipodal sets): do not compare dec/inc (noise on both sides); a95 (180), k and csd remain comparable.
Pole mean (PB-05 reuse): Direction(poleLongitude, poleLatitude, 1) -> [lon, lat] pairs with no rounding (Graphs.tsx:26-30); the same k/'inf' and N<2 rules apply.
convention_differences: Declination normalisation: PMTools adds 2pi when atan2 < 0 (Coordinates.ts:47-49); PmagPy uses (arctan2/rad) % 360 (pmag.py:2615). Same range [0, 360), last-ULP differences only.
k when R == N: PMTools number Infinity (calculateFisherMean.ts:64); PmagPy string 'inf' (pmag.py:4489).
N < 2: PmagPy returns {'dec','inc'} only (pmag.py:4465-4467); PMTools computes a95 = NaN (20^(1/0) - 1 = Infinity, times (N-R) = 0 gives NaN) and k = Infinity.

final.thesis_agreement: Matches. thesis.txt:348-363 (section 1.3) gives formula (1.4) k = (N-1)/(N-R) and formula (1.5) alpha(1-p) = arccos(1 - (N-R)/R * ((1/p)^(1/(N-1)) - 1)) with p = 0.05, i.e. 1/p = 20; calculateFisherMean.ts:61 and 68-71 implement exactly these with the constant 20 (and pmag.py:4486, 4492-4494 likewise). The thesis does not describe csd = 81/sqrt(k), the a < -1 clamp, the a < 0 -> 180 rule, the 0.1-degree input rounding or the user polarity flip; those come from the PmagPy port (comment at calculateFisherMean.ts:38) and from calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:23-30. UI chapter: thesis.txt:1009-1012 lists the FISHER method button; thesis.txt:1049-1052 says the results table shows 'MAD or a95 and k' (so the shared MAD column for a95 is by design); thesis.txt:1074-1078 says the VGP stereogram automatically shows the Fisher mean, matching Graphs.tsx:25-42 and dataToStereoVGP.ts:55-85.
final.confidence_reason: Every claim rests on opened source lines (PMTools and pmag.py/ipmag.py 4.3.14) and on 20 identical-input runs plus two targeted probes (rounding-tie emulation on 14 values; R == N behaviour on 30 identical-direction sets), all reproduced from scripts kept in the scratchpad (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-i1948374-PMTools/bdb3b478-28ac-4114-92f5-3720a2d0303d/scratchpad/PB-02-map/oracle.py, compare.py, py_round.py, py_rn.py, pmtools_results.json, pmagpy_results.json). The PMTools function is a literal port of pmag.fisher_mean and the observed maximum difference outside degenerate inputs is 5.7e-14. Not verified: behaviour of the CSV/XLSX/MDIR DIR parsers for negative or multi-decimal declinations (only relevant to the fmod and rounding adapter notes), and the VGP cache contents beyond the rounding lines cited (PB-05's scope).

mapping.pmtools_method: Inputs: the selected PMD steps' Cartesian x,y,z in SPECIMEN (core) coordinates as parsed from the file (parserPMD.ts:46-54; Xc,Yc,Zc columns in Am2), selected by 1-based index in file order (calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:12). No rounding, no polarity flip, no hemisphere flip of inputs. Preprocessing per mode (calculatePCA_pmd.ts): (1) 'gcn' only: each step divided by its own length (line 19-20), so unit vectors; other modes keep intensity weights. (2) 'pca' only (anchored=false): subtract the centre of mass cm = mean of vectors (lines 29-41). 'pca0', 'gc', 'gcn' are NOT centred (matrix through the origin). Orientation matrix T = sum_i v_i v_i^T / N (matrix.ts:62-66). Eigen-decomposition with numeric.eig; eigenvalues divided by trace (eigManipulations.ts:10-19) so tau1+tau2+tau3 = 1 and sorted descending (lines 34-40). Line modes ('pca','pca0'): direction = eigenvector v1 (tau max); sign chosen so that v1 . (first_step - last_step) >= 0, i.e. reflect when the dot is < 0 (line 47, 54); MAD = atan( sqrt(tau2+tau3) / sqrt(tau1) ) in degrees (lines 61-62) = thesis formula (1.1). Plane modes ('gc','gcn'): direction shown = pole = eigenvector v3 (tau min); sign chosen so that z <= 0 in the specimen frame (reflect when z > 0, line 55), i.e. the pole is forced into the upper hemisphere in SPECIMEN coordinates, before any rotation; MAD = atan( sqrt(tau3/tau2 + tau3/tau1) ) in degrees (lines 68-69) = thesis formula (1.2). Non-finite MAD (NaN/Infinity from zero eigenvalues) is replaced by 0 (lines 63, 70). Output: component.edges (unit eigenvector, specimen frame), component.centerMass (zero vector unless 'pca'), intensity = |first - last| (unused), MAD. The formatter then rotates edges to geographic via rotateTo(a,b) and to stratigraphic via correctBedding(s,d) (PB-01 territory) and rounds everything shown to 0.1 degree. Constants: RADIANS = 180/pi. No iteration beyond the eigen solver, no randomness. Units: degrees for all shown angles. Declination in [0,360): a value such as 359.99999999997 is shown as 360.0 after toFixed(1) (observed in the dec-wrap edge case), PmagPy keeps the same unrounded number.

mapping.verdict_explanation: One row hides four methods and the proposed oracle covers only two of them exactly. (a) 'pca' = pmag.domean DE-BFL: identical algorithm (centred intensity-weighted T, same sign rule v1.(first-last)>=0, same MAD formula); float-noise agreement on 7 real cases: |ddec| <= 5.7e-14, |dinc| <= 5.0e-14, |dMAD| <= 3.5e-13 deg. (b) 'pca0' = anchored PCA (thesis: centre of mass at the origin, thesis.txt:1289-1291): the MAD equals DE-BFL-A specimen_mad to 4.4e-13 deg, but DE-BFL-A's direction is pmag.vector_mean (pmag.py:2983), a different estimator that PmagPy itself flags as unverified (2995); on real data it differs from PMTools' eigenvector by 0.02-13.8 deg (7.85 deg dec / 12.3 deg inc on examplePCA M070-M130). PMTools' pca0 direction is instead reproduced to 5.7e-14 deg by pmag.doprinc([dec,inc,int]).dec/inc compared as an axis, and bit-for-bit (2e-16) by pmag.Tmatrix+pmag.tauV with the first-last sign applied. (c) 'gcn' = DE-BFP: identical (uncentred unit vectors, same plane MAD); agreement 1.4e-10/4.7e-11/2.1e-10 deg, but the PmagPy pole has no sign rule (pmag.py:3033) while PMTools forces z<=0 in the specimen frame (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:55): 3 of 7 real cases came back antipodal, so the test must compare axes or flip the PmagPy pole to inc<=0. (d) 'gc' (intensity-weighted plane through the origin) has NO domean equivalent: DE-BFP silently drops intensities (pmag.py:2927), giving up to 50.4 deg axis and 15.3 deg MAD difference; the correct oracle is pmag.doprinc([dec,inc,int]).V3dec/V3inc (axis) with MAD from its tau1..3 via thesis formula (1.2), which agrees to 1.5e-10 deg. Frame: PMTools fits in specimen coordinates and rotates the eigenvector afterwards; the fit is rotation-invariant so the parity test should compare in specimen coordinates and leave the rotation to PB-01. Nothing in this row is a PMTools science bug; the mismatch is between the plan's oracle choice and what PmagPy actually computes.

adapters_required: Input: PMTools step (x, y, z) in specimen frame -> pmag.cart2dir([x,y,z]) -> row [treatment_index, dec, inc, intensity, '', 'g']; call domean(rows, 0, N-1, type) on exactly the selected steps in FILE order (PMTools filters by index, calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:12). Zero-length steps cannot be expressed (cart2dir gives NaN -> LinAlgError), skip or assert them separately.

Mode map: pca -> 'DE-BFL'; pca0 -> MAD from 'DE-BFL-A' + direction from doprinc([dec,inc,int]) (or Tmatrix+tauV v1); gcn -> 'DE-BFP'; gc -> doprinc([dec,inc,int]) V3 + thesis (1.2) on tau. Do NOT map gc to DE-BFP and do NOT take the DE-BFL-A direction.

Sign adapters: lines: PmagPy DE-BFL already uses v1.(first-last)>=0, no adapter; doprinc directions are lower-hemisphere (doflip) -> compare as axes or antipode-align to PMTools' first-last choice. Planes: PmagPy DE-BFP pole sign is arbitrary -> flip to inc<=0 (PMTools convention is z<=0 in the specimen frame) or compare as axes; doprinc V3 is lower-hemisphere -> take the antipode.
Declination comparison modulo 360 (PMTools can emit 359.9999999999 vs 0); compare unrounded specimen-frame values; the UI rounds to 0.1.
Compare in specimen coordinates (feed x,y,z directly); geographic/stratigraphic values go through PB-01's rotation oracle (dogeo/dotilt), not through PB-03.

Avoid inputs with exactly tied eigenvalues: pmag.tauV reports t2 = 0 on exact ties (pmag.py:2681-2683), e.g. three orthogonal unit vectors give PmagPy MAD 45 vs PMTools 54.7 (and 0 vs 45 for the centred fit); neither value is meaningful and this is a PmagPy quirk, not a PMTools defect.

scripts/gen_pca.py already builds the 6-column rows and calls domean (lines 55-61); it must be extended to call doprinc for gc/pca0-direction, and its README claim that DE-BFL-A 'matches calculatePCA_pmd(anchored=true)' (scripts/README.md:128-129) must be corrected to 'MAD only'.
convention_differences: Plane weighting: PmagPy DE-BFP forces intensity 1.0 (pmag.py:2927); PMTools gc keeps intensities, gcn normalises (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:19). gcn == DE-BFP; gc has no domean equivalent.

Anchored line direction: PMTools pca0 = eigenvector of the uncentred T (thesis.txt:1289-1291 'centre of mass at the origin'); PmagPy DE-BFL-A = vector_mean (pmag.py:2983) with its own 'check' comment (2995). MAD formulas coincide.

Plane pole sign: PMTools forces z<=0 (upper hemisphere) in the SPECIMEN frame before rotation (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:55), so Igeo/Istrat of a pole may be positive; PmagPy DE-BFP leaves the LAPACK sign (3033); doprinc forces the lower hemisphere (doflip).

Line sign: identical rule on both sides (v1 . (first - last) >= 0; calculatePCA_pmd.ts:54 vs pmag.py:3010-3024). When the dot is exactly 0 both sides keep the solver's arbitrary sign (observed in the synthetic 'horizontal pole' case: PMTools 180/-45 vs tauV 0/45).
T matrix scaling: PMTools divides by N (matrix.ts:65), PmagPy does not (2714); irrelevant after trace normalisation (eigManipulations.ts:18, pmag.py:2670).

Degenerate eigenvalues: PMTools replaces non-finite MAD with 0 (lines 63, 70) and can return a tiny noise MAD (6e-6 deg for gcn on a rank-1 set); PmagPy clamps only t3<0 (2980-2981) and can return NaN or a garbage MAD (24.57 deg for DE-BFP with N=1). Exact eigenvalue ties: PMTools indexOf picks duplicate indices, PmagPy tauV sets t2=0.

Frame of the fit: PmagPy fits whatever frame the datablock is in (zeq_magic passes coord 's'/'g'/'t' data); PMTools always fits in specimen coordinates and rotates the eigenvector (rawStatisticsPMDToInterpretation.ts:20-30). Rotation-invariant except for the pole sign noted above.
Display: PMTools rounds to 0.1 deg and can show declination 360.0; PmagPy returns unrounded values modulo 360.
N=1: unreachable in PMTools UI (InterpretationSetter.tsx:47 requires >= 2 steps); calculatePCA_pmd('pca') throws 'eig: internal error' there, PmagPy DE-BFL returns direction_type 'Error'.

mapping.thesis_agreement: Code matches the thesis. Formulas: thesis.txt:318-323 (1.1) MAD = arctan(sqrt((lambda_int + lambda_min)/lambda_max)) == calculatePCA_pmd.ts:61-62; thesis.txt:325-329 (1.2) MAD = arctan(sqrt(lambda_min/lambda_int + lambda_min/lambda_max)) == lines 68-69; thesis.txt:331-345 (1.3) H built from (x_i - x_mean) etc. == centred T for 'pca' (lines 29-41, matrix.ts:56-71; the thesis omits the 1/N, which cancels after trace normalisation). UI semantics: thesis.txt:862-866 lists PCA, PCA0 ('with anchoring to the origin'), GC, GCN ('with normalisation of the input vector lengths'); thesis.txt:1289-1293 says PCA0 = principal components 'with the centre of mass at the origin', PCA = unchanged == anchored flag (calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:18); thesis.txt:1297-1305 says GC keeps the vector lengths as weights and GCN sets all weights to one == normalized flag (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:19-20, calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:23-27). The thesis does not state whether the GC/GCN plane is centred (code: through the origin, like PmagPy DE-BFP), nor the line-sign rule (code: first minus last) or the pole-sign rule (code: upper hemisphere in specimen frame); these are code conventions, not thesis requirements. FZE0150.txt was not needed for this row (not opened).

final.pmtools_method: Inputs: the selected PMD steps' Cartesian x,y,z in SPECIMEN (core) coordinates as parsed from the file (parserPMD.ts:46-54; Xc,Yc,Zc columns in Am2), selected by 1-based index in file order (calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:12). No rounding, no polarity flip, no hemisphere flip of inputs. Preprocessing per mode (calculatePCA_pmd.ts): (1) 'gcn' only: each step divided by its own length (line 19-20), so unit vectors; other modes keep intensity weights. (2) 'pca' only (anchored=false): subtract the centre of mass cm = mean of vectors (lines 29-41). 'pca0', 'gc', 'gcn' are NOT centred (matrix through the origin). Orientation matrix T = sum_i v_i v_i^T / N (matrix.ts:62-66). Eigen-decomposition with numeric.eig; eigenvalues divided by trace (eigManipulations.ts:10-19) so tau1+tau2+tau3 = 1 and sorted descending (lines 34-40). Line modes ('pca','pca0'): direction = eigenvector v1 (tau max); sign chosen so that v1 . (first_step - last_step) >= 0, i.e. reflect when the dot is < 0 (line 47, 54); MAD = atan( sqrt(tau2+tau3) / sqrt(tau1) ) in degrees (lines 61-62) = thesis formula (1.1). Plane modes ('gc','gcn'): direction shown = pole = eigenvector v3 (tau min); sign chosen so that z <= 0 in the specimen frame (reflect when z > 0, line 55), i.e. the pole is forced into the upper hemisphere in SPECIMEN coordinates, before any rotation; MAD = atan( sqrt(tau3/tau2 + tau3/tau1) ) in degrees (lines 68-69) = thesis formula (1.2). Non-finite MAD (NaN/Infinity from zero eigenvalues) is replaced by 0 (lines 63, 70). Output: component.edges (unit eigenvector, specimen frame), component.centerMass (zero vector unless 'pca'), intensity = |first - last| (unused), MAD. The formatter then rotates edges to geographic via rotateTo(a,b) and to stratigraphic via correctBedding(s,d) (PB-01 territory) and rounds everything shown to 0.1 degree. Constants: RADIANS = 180/pi. No iteration beyond the eigen solver, no randomness. Units: degrees for all shown angles. Declination in [0,360): a value such as 359.99999999997 is shown as 360.0 after toFixed(1) (observed in the dec-wrap edge case), PmagPy keeps the same unrounded number.

pmagpy_oracles.method: Centre on mean of the N points (2951-2963), T = Tmatrix = sum v v^T (no /N, 2692-2717), tauV: numpy.linalg.eig, eigenvalues divided by trace (2670), sorted descending (2674-2683); v1 sign so that v1 . (P_start - P_end) >= 0 (3010-3024); MAD = atan(sqrt(t2+t3)/sqrt(t1)) (3029); t3 clamped to 0 if negative (2980-2981). Identical to PMTools 'pca'.

pmagpy_oracles.input_format: same; intensities used
pmagpy_oracles.outputs: specimen_dec/inc = pmag.vector_mean(fdata) i.e. direction of the RESULTANT SUM of the step vectors (1660-1693), NOT the eigenvector; specimen_mad = atan(sqrt(t2+t3)/sqrt(t1)) from the UNCENTRED T; no specimen_dang; specimen_n
pmagpy_oracles.method: No centring (2960 excludes DE-BFL-A), T of raw vectors, eigenvalues as above. PmagPy's own comment at 2995: 'I think this is how it is done - i never anchor the "PCA" - check'. So only the MAD is a true anchored-PCA quantity; the direction is a different estimator.

pmagpy_oracles.input_format: same, but intensity is IGNORED: every point is built as [dec, inc, 1.0] (2927), i.e. unit vectors
pmagpy_oracles.outputs: specimen_dec/inc = pole = eigenvector v3 with NO sign rule (sign is whatever numpy.linalg.eig returns; observed both hemispheres); specimen_mad = atan(sqrt(t3/t2 + t3/t1)); specimen_dang (meaningless, ~90); specimen_n; specimen_direction_type 'p'
pmagpy_oracles.method: Uncentred T of unit vectors; identical to PMTools 'gcn' up to the pole sign.
pmagpy_oracles.role: primary for mode 'gcn' (plane on unit vectors) with a sign adapter; NOT an oracle for 'gc' (intensity-weighted): differs by up to 50 deg axis / 15 deg MAD on real data

pmagpy_oracles.signature: doprinc(data) -> {dec, inc, V2dec, V2inc, V3dec, V3inc, tau1, tau2, tau3, N}
pmagpy_oracles.input_format: list of [dec, inc] or [dec, inc, intensity]; with intensity the vectors are NOT unit, so T is the intensity-weighted uncentred matrix
pmagpy_oracles.outputs: dec/inc = v1 flipped to LOWER hemisphere by doflip (6146-6167: inc<0 -> antipode); V3dec/V3inc = v3 also flipped to lower hemisphere; tau1..3 trace-normalised eigenvalues; no MAD
pmagpy_oracles.method: Uncentred T of dir2cart(data). With [dec,inc,int] rows its v1 is exactly the thesis/Kirschvink anchored-PCA eigenvector (PMTools 'pca0', up to sign) and its v3 is the intensity-weighted plane pole (PMTools 'gc', up to sign); MAD must be computed from tau1..3 with thesis formulas (1.1)/(1.2). Verified on 7 real cases: |ddec|,|dinc| <= 1.5e-10, |dMAD| <= 1.4e-10 deg.
pmagpy_oracles.role: primary for mode 'gc' (axis + tau) and secondary oracle for the 'pca0' direction (axis); sign adapter required (PMTools line sign = first-last rule, plane pole z<=0 in specimen frame; doprinc = lower hemisphere)

pmagpy_oracles.qualified_name: pmag.Tmatrix + pmag.tauV on raw Cartesian rows
pmagpy_oracles.input_format: raw Cartesian rows (x,y,z), no dir2cart round trip
pmagpy_oracles.outputs: t trace-normalised sorted eigenvalues; V eigenvectors (rows of transpose(eig vectors)), arbitrary sign
pmagpy_oracles.method: Same algebra as PMTools TMatrix+sortEigenvectors (which eigManipulations.ts:28 says was 'taken from the PmagPY library'); differs only by the /N (cancels after trace normalisation). Verified: max |edges - v| <= 2e-12 on all real cases after applying PMTools' sign rules in the test.
pmagpy_oracles.role: helper: exact-algebra oracle for 'pca0' and 'gc' when the test wants to avoid the dec/inc round trip

final.verdict_explanation: One row hides four methods and the proposed oracle covers only two of them exactly. (a) 'pca' = pmag.domean DE-BFL: identical algorithm (centred intensity-weighted T, same sign rule v1.(first-last)>=0, same MAD formula); float-noise agreement on 7 real cases: |ddec| <= 5.7e-14, |dinc| <= 5.0e-14, |dMAD| <= 3.5e-13 deg. (b) 'pca0' = anchored PCA (thesis: centre of mass at the origin, thesis.txt:1289-1291): the MAD equals DE-BFL-A specimen_mad to 4.4e-13 deg, but DE-BFL-A's direction is pmag.vector_mean (pmag.py:2983), a different estimator that PmagPy itself flags as unverified (2995); on real data it differs from PMTools' eigenvector by 0.02-13.8 deg (7.85 deg dec / 12.3 deg inc on examplePCA M070-M130). PMTools' pca0 direction is instead reproduced to 5.7e-14 deg by pmag.doprinc([dec,inc,int]).dec/inc compared as an axis, and bit-for-bit (2e-16) by pmag.Tmatrix+pmag.tauV with the first-last sign applied. (c) 'gcn' = DE-BFP: identical (uncentred unit vectors, same plane MAD); agreement 1.4e-10/4.7e-11/2.1e-10 deg, but the PmagPy pole has no sign rule (pmag.py:3033) while PMTools forces z<=0 in the specimen frame (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:55): 3 of 7 real cases came back antipodal, so the test must compare axes or flip the PmagPy pole to inc<=0. (d) 'gc' (intensity-weighted plane through the origin) has NO domean equivalent: DE-BFP silently drops intensities (pmag.py:2927), giving up to 50.4 deg axis and 15.3 deg MAD difference; the correct oracle is pmag.doprinc([dec,inc,int]).V3dec/V3inc (axis) with MAD from its tau1..3 via thesis formula (1.2), which agrees to 1.5e-10 deg. Frame: PMTools fits in specimen coordinates and rotates the eigenvector afterwards; the fit is rotation-invariant so the parity test should compare in specimen coordinates and leave the rotation to PB-01. Nothing in this row is a PMTools science bug; the mismatch is between the plan's oracle choice and what PmagPy actually computes.

adapters_required: Input: PMTools step (x, y, z) in specimen frame -> pmag.cart2dir([x,y,z]) -> row [treatment_index, dec, inc, intensity, '', 'g']; call domean(rows, 0, N-1, type) on exactly the selected steps in FILE order (PMTools filters by index, calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:12). Zero-length steps cannot be expressed (cart2dir gives NaN -> LinAlgError), skip or assert them separately.

Mode map: pca -> 'DE-BFL'; pca0 -> MAD from 'DE-BFL-A' + direction from doprinc([dec,inc,int]) (or Tmatrix+tauV v1); gcn -> 'DE-BFP'; gc -> doprinc([dec,inc,int]) V3 + thesis (1.2) on tau. Do NOT map gc to DE-BFP and do NOT take the DE-BFL-A direction.

Sign adapters: lines: PmagPy DE-BFL already uses v1.(first-last)>=0, no adapter; doprinc directions are lower-hemisphere (doflip) -> compare as axes or antipode-align to PMTools' first-last choice. Planes: PmagPy DE-BFP pole sign is arbitrary -> flip to inc<=0 (PMTools convention is z<=0 in the specimen frame) or compare as axes; doprinc V3 is lower-hemisphere -> take the antipode.
Declination comparison modulo 360 (PMTools can emit 359.9999999999 vs 0); compare unrounded specimen-frame values; the UI rounds to 0.1.
Compare in specimen coordinates (feed x,y,z directly); geographic/stratigraphic values go through PB-01's rotation oracle (dogeo/dotilt), not through PB-03.

Avoid inputs with exactly tied eigenvalues: pmag.tauV reports t2 = 0 on exact ties (pmag.py:2681-2683), e.g. three orthogonal unit vectors give PmagPy MAD 45 vs PMTools 54.7 (and 0 vs 45 for the centred fit); neither value is meaningful and this is a PmagPy quirk, not a PMTools defect.

scripts/gen_pca.py already builds the 6-column rows and calls domean (lines 55-61); it must be extended to call doprinc for gc/pca0-direction, and its README claim that DE-BFL-A 'matches calculatePCA_pmd(anchored=true)' (scripts/README.md:128-129) must be corrected to 'MAD only'.
convention_differences: Plane weighting: PmagPy DE-BFP forces intensity 1.0 (pmag.py:2927); PMTools gc keeps intensities, gcn normalises (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:19). gcn == DE-BFP; gc has no domean equivalent.

Anchored line direction: PMTools pca0 = eigenvector of the uncentred T (thesis.txt:1289-1291 'centre of mass at the origin'); PmagPy DE-BFL-A = vector_mean (pmag.py:2983) with its own 'check' comment (2995). MAD formulas coincide.

Plane pole sign: PMTools forces z<=0 (upper hemisphere) in the SPECIMEN frame before rotation (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:55), so Igeo/Istrat of a pole may be positive; PmagPy DE-BFP leaves the LAPACK sign (3033); doprinc forces the lower hemisphere (doflip).

Line sign: identical rule on both sides (v1 . (first - last) >= 0; calculatePCA_pmd.ts:54 vs pmag.py:3010-3024). When the dot is exactly 0 both sides keep the solver's arbitrary sign (observed in the synthetic 'horizontal pole' case: PMTools 180/-45 vs tauV 0/45).
T matrix scaling: PMTools divides by N (matrix.ts:65), PmagPy does not (2714); irrelevant after trace normalisation (eigManipulations.ts:18, pmag.py:2670).

Degenerate eigenvalues: PMTools replaces non-finite MAD with 0 (lines 63, 70) and can return a tiny noise MAD (6e-6 deg for gcn on a rank-1 set); PmagPy clamps only t3<0 (2980-2981) and can return NaN or a garbage MAD (24.57 deg for DE-BFP with N=1). Exact eigenvalue ties: PMTools indexOf picks duplicate indices, PmagPy tauV sets t2=0.

Frame of the fit: PmagPy fits whatever frame the datablock is in (zeq_magic passes coord 's'/'g'/'t' data); PMTools always fits in specimen coordinates and rotates the eigenvector (rawStatisticsPMDToInterpretation.ts:20-30). Rotation-invariant except for the pole sign noted above.
Display: PMTools rounds to 0.1 deg and can show declination 360.0; PmagPy returns unrounded values modulo 360.
N=1: unreachable in PMTools UI (InterpretationSetter.tsx:47 requires >= 2 steps); calculatePCA_pmd('pca') throws 'eig: internal error' there, PmagPy DE-BFL returns direction_type 'Error'.

final.thesis_agreement: Code matches the thesis. Formulas: thesis.txt:318-323 (1.1) MAD = arctan(sqrt((lambda_int + lambda_min)/lambda_max)) == calculatePCA_pmd.ts:61-62; thesis.txt:325-329 (1.2) MAD = arctan(sqrt(lambda_min/lambda_int + lambda_min/lambda_max)) == lines 68-69; thesis.txt:331-345 (1.3) H built from (x_i - x_mean) etc. == centred T for 'pca' (lines 29-41, matrix.ts:56-71; the thesis omits the 1/N, which cancels after trace normalisation). UI semantics: thesis.txt:862-866 lists PCA, PCA0 ('with anchoring to the origin'), GC, GCN ('with normalisation of the input vector lengths'); thesis.txt:1289-1293 says PCA0 = principal components 'with the centre of mass at the origin', PCA = unchanged == anchored flag (calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:18); thesis.txt:1297-1305 says GC keeps the vector lengths as weights and GCN sets all weights to one == normalized flag (calculatePCA_pmd.ts:19-20, calculateStatisticsPMD.ts:23-27). The thesis does not state whether the GC/GCN plane is centred (code: through the origin, like PmagPy DE-BFP), nor the line-sign rule (code: first minus last) or the pole-sign rule (code: upper hemisphere in specimen frame); these are code conventions, not thesis requirements. FZE0150.txt was not needed for this row (not opened).

mapping.pmtools_method: Inputs: the selected DIR rows' Dgeo/Igeo and Dstrat/Istrat in degrees (D east of north, I positive down). Preprocessing (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:17-38): rows whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs are antipoded (Direction.reversePolarity: dec+180 mod 360, -inc; Direction.ts:62-68), then all four angles are rounded to 0.1 deg with toFixed(1) (:27-30). Per frame (pcaByReference, calculatePCA_dir.ts:21-69): unit vectors x = (cos D cos I, sin D cos I, sin I) (Direction.ts:28-38, z down); the vector list is duplicated verbatim (:44, a no-op); orientation matrix T = (1/N) sum x x^T, NOT centred (matrix.ts:56-71; the centerMass variable at :24 is never applied); numeric.eig(T); eigenvalues divided by the trace and sorted descending tau1 >= tau2 >= tau3 with eigenvectors v1, v2, v3 (eigManipulations.ts:7-20, :23-61). Result direction = v3 (the pole of the best-fit plane through the origin = pole of the best-fit great circle through the selected directions; when the selected rows are great-circle poles this is their least-squares common intersection point); if v3.z > 0 the vector is negated (:56), so the reported pole always has inclination <= 0 (upper hemisphere; z == 0 is left as the eigensolver returned it). dec = atan2(y,x) mapped to [0,360), inc = asin(z/|v|) (Coordinates.ts:39-52). MAD = atan(sqrt(tau3/tau2 + tau3/tau1)) in degrees, replaced by 0 when NaN or +/-Infinity (:61-63; thesis formula 1..2). Identical computation for geographic and stratigraphic. No k, R, N, no iteration, no randomness, no constants beyond 180/pi. Because T is invariant under x -> -x, polarity reversal of individual rows does not change the result (verified numerically). The formatter rounds the direction and MAD to 0.1 deg for the tables (rawStatisticsDIRToInterpretation.ts:35-42) and stores the raw values in rawData; Kgeo/Kstrat are shown as 0.

mapping.verdict_explanation: PMTools' DIR-page GC mode is a least-squares plane through the origin fitted to the unit vectors of the selected directions, reported as the plane's pole (minimum eigenvector of the uncentred orientation matrix) in the upper hemisphere, with the Kirschvink plane MAD. pmag.doprinc builds the same matrix (its sum vs PMTools' 1/N-weighted sum cancels in the trace normalisation both sides apply) and returns the same axis as V3dec/V3inc, but flipped to the lower hemisphere and without a MAD. pmag.domean(..., 'DE-BFP') uses the identical MAD formula (pmag.py:3019) on the same eigenvalues. On 16 inputs (test-data/sample.dir in both frames with and without polarity flips, N=2, declination wrap, vertical/horizontal poles, scattered poles) the pole agrees with the antipode of doprinc's V3 to <= 2.3e-13 deg and the MAD agrees with domean's specimen_mad to <= 8e-13 deg (2.5e-7 deg at N=2 where tau3 is float noise). The only regimes without agreement are mathematically degenerate (rank-1 T: identical or exactly antipodal directions, or N=1), where neither side defines a pole and PMTools reports a noise-driven MAD while PmagPy clamps to 0; and the exactly-horizontal-pole boundary (inc == 0 within noise) where the hemisphere choice is undefined on both sides and the comparison must be as an axis. Plan row needs to name both oracles (doprinc for the axis, domean DE-BFP for the MAD) and the hemisphere adapter.

adapters_required: Inputs to PmagPy must be the values PMTools actually uses: polarity-reversed rows antipoded and all angles rounded to 0.1 deg (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:21-30); .dir inputs are already 0.1 deg so this is a no-op for them, not for CSV/XLSX with more decimals.

doprinc input: nested list [[dec, inc], ...] (2 columns -> unit vectors, pmag.py:2783-2790). domean input: rows [index, dec, inc, 1.0, '', 'g'], start=0, end=N-1, pass copy.deepcopy (domean mutates rows, pmag.py:2896), calculation_type 'DE-BFP'.

Hemisphere: PMTools pole has inc <= 0 (calculatePCA_dir.ts:56 reflects when z > 0); doprinc V3 has inc >= 0 (doflip pmag.py:6527); domean DE-BFP v3 sign is whatever numpy returns (pmag.py:3018). Adapter: antipode the oracle direction when its inc > 0; assert by angle between vectors, and as an axis (mod 180) when |inc| < ~1e-6 deg.

MAD: take domean DE-BFP 'specimen_mad' (clamps tau3 < 0 to 0, pmag.py:2974-2975) or compute atan(sqrt(t3/t2+t3/t1)) from doprinc tau with max(tau3, 0); PMTools maps a non-finite result to 0 (calculatePCA_dir.ts:63). Use tolerance ~1e-5 deg when N = 2 (tau3 is pure noise), 1e-9 otherwise.
Run the oracle twice per case: on (Dgeo, Igeo) and on (Dstrat, Istrat); PMTools returns both frames from one call.

Skip or treat as degenerate any case whose orientation matrix is rank 1 (N = 1, all directions identical, or all exactly antipodal): numpy returns complex eigenvalues (observed: (1+0j, -2.5e-17+2.1e-17j, ...)) and the pole is arbitrary on both sides. N = 1 is unreachable from the UI (InterpretationSetter.tsx:50 requires >= 2).

Avoid synthetic inputs with exactly equal eigenvalues: tauV picks the middle eigenvalue with `!=` (pmag.py:2686-2688), leaving t2 = 0 and ind2 = 1 on exact ties, which breaks the oracle's MAD (division by zero) while PMTools' indexOf-based sort still returns a value.
convention_differences: Pole hemisphere: PMTools upper (negative inclination; calculatePCA_dir.ts:56, same convention as the PCA page's plane fit calculatePCA_pmd.ts:55) vs doprinc lower (pmag.py:6512-6528 via doflip) vs domean DE-BFP unnormalised (pmag.py:3018).

Orientation-matrix scale: PMTools TMatrix divides each product by N (matrix.ts:65); pmag.Tmatrix does not (pmag.py:2713). Irrelevant after both sides divide the eigenvalues by the trace (eigManipulations.ts:7-20; pmag.py:2674-2677).

Centring: neither side centres for this fit (PMTools: centerMass declared at calculatePCA_dir.ts:24 but never subtracted; PmagPy: DE-BFP excluded from centring at pmag.py:2954-2960; doprinc never centres). The thesis matrix 1..3 (thesis.txt:331-345) is the centred covariance H, which applies to the PCA-page line fit, not to a great circle through the origin.

Negative tau3 noise: domean clamps to 0 (pmag.py:2974-2975); doprinc does not clamp (tau3 = -4e-17 observed at N=2); PMTools does not clamp but replaces a NaN/Infinity MAD by 0 (calculatePCA_dir.ts:63).

Input rounding: PMTools rounds inputs to 0.1 deg before fitting (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:27-30) and outputs to 0.1 deg in the tables (rawStatisticsDIRToInterpretation.ts:35-42); PmagPy rounds nothing.

Polarity flags: PMTools antipodes reversed rows first (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:23-26); the fit is invariant to this (T is sign-invariant), verified: sample.dir with rows 2,4,6,8 reversed gives the same pole to 1.7e-13 deg.

Declination at a vertical pole is arbitrary on both sides (PMTools 180, doprinc 0 for all-horizontal directions); tie-breaking of the hemisphere at an exactly horizontal pole depends on the eigensolver's sign noise on both sides (PMTools reflects only when z > 0, doprinc flips only when inc < 0).
Extra PmagPy outputs with no PMTools counterpart: V1/V2 directions, specimen_dang (angle centre-of-mass to pole); extra PMTools display with no PmagPy counterpart: Kgeo/Kstrat = 0.

mapping.thesis_agreement: Partly. The MAD formula in the code (calculatePCA_dir.ts:61-62, atan sqrt(lambda_min/lambda_int + lambda_min/lambda_max)) is exactly thesis formula (1..2) for planes (thesis.txt:325-329). The thesis defines the eigenvalues on the centred matrix H (formula 1..3, thesis.txt:331-345), but the DIR-page GC code uses the uncentred orientation matrix T = (1/N) sum x x^T (matrix.ts:56-71; centerMass at calculatePCA_dir.ts:24 is never applied). For a great circle, i.e. a plane through the origin of the unit sphere, the uncentred matrix is the correct one and it is what PmagPy uses for DE-BFP (pmag.py:2954-2960 skips centring for planes) and in doprinc (pmag.py:6505); the thesis's centred H describes the PCA-page line fit. The thesis describes the DIR-page GC as 'the intersection of remagnetisation circles' (thesis.txt:1011-1013) without a formula; the minimum eigenvector of the orientation matrix of the circles' poles is the least-squares common intersection point, so the code matches that wording. The thesis also lists a GCN method on the DIR page (thesis.txt:1013) that the app does not implement (only a hotkey that stores zeros). The results table description (thesis.txt:1049-1052: Dgeo/Igeo, Dstrat/Istrat, MAD or a95 and k) matches the columns shown. The hemisphere convention (pole reported with inclination <= 0) is not stated in the thesis: not verified against any text.
mapping.confidence_reason: Every claim rests on opened source lines (PMTools TypeScript and pmagpy 4.3.14 pmag.py/ipmag.py, version confirmed at version.py:7) and on runs of both implementations on identical inputs: 16 cases in two frames, with agreement at the 1e-13 deg level for the pole and <= 8e-13 deg for the MAD wherever the problem is non-degenerate, and eigenvalue parity at 2.8e-16. The UI click path for 'gc' and the 'gcn' hotkey were traced by reading (not by driving the browser); the 'gcn' zero result was reproduced by calling the dispatcher directly. The hemisphere convention has no thesis statement to check against.

final.pmtools_method: Inputs: the selected DIR rows' Dgeo/Igeo and Dstrat/Istrat in degrees (D east of north, I positive down). Preprocessing (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:17-38): rows whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs are antipoded (Direction.reversePolarity: dec+180 mod 360, -inc; Direction.ts:62-68), then all four angles are rounded to 0.1 deg with toFixed(1) (:27-30). Per frame (pcaByReference, calculatePCA_dir.ts:21-69): unit vectors x = (cos D cos I, sin D cos I, sin I) (Direction.ts:28-38, z down); the vector list is duplicated verbatim (:44, a no-op); orientation matrix T = (1/N) sum x x^T, NOT centred (matrix.ts:56-71; the centerMass variable at :24 is never applied); numeric.eig(T); eigenvalues divided by the trace and sorted descending tau1 >= tau2 >= tau3 with eigenvectors v1, v2, v3 (eigManipulations.ts:7-20, :23-61). Result direction = v3 (the pole of the best-fit plane through the origin = pole of the best-fit great circle through the selected directions; when the selected rows are great-circle poles this is their least-squares common intersection point); if v3.z > 0 the vector is negated (:56), so the reported pole always has inclination <= 0 (upper hemisphere; z == 0 is left as the eigensolver returned it). dec = atan2(y,x) mapped to [0,360), inc = asin(z/|v|) (Coordinates.ts:39-52). MAD = atan(sqrt(tau3/tau2 + tau3/tau1)) in degrees, replaced by 0 when NaN or +/-Infinity (:61-63; thesis formula 1..2). Identical computation for geographic and stratigraphic. No k, R, N, no iteration, no randomness, no constants beyond 180/pi. Because T is invariant under x -> -x, polarity reversal of individual rows does not change the result (verified numerically). The formatter rounds the direction and MAD to 0.1 deg for the tables (rawStatisticsDIRToInterpretation.ts:35-42) and stores the raw values in rawData; Kgeo/Kstrat are shown as 0.

final.verdict_explanation: PMTools' DIR-page GC mode is a least-squares plane through the origin fitted to the unit vectors of the selected directions, reported as the plane's pole (minimum eigenvector of the uncentred orientation matrix) in the upper hemisphere, with the Kirschvink plane MAD. pmag.doprinc builds the same matrix (its sum vs PMTools' 1/N-weighted sum cancels in the trace normalisation both sides apply) and returns the same axis as V3dec/V3inc, but flipped to the lower hemisphere and without a MAD. pmag.domean(..., 'DE-BFP') uses the identical MAD formula (pmag.py:3019) on the same eigenvalues. On 16 inputs (test-data/sample.dir in both frames with and without polarity flips, N=2, declination wrap, vertical/horizontal poles, scattered poles) the pole agrees with the antipode of doprinc's V3 to <= 2.3e-13 deg and the MAD agrees with domean's specimen_mad to <= 8e-13 deg (2.5e-7 deg at N=2 where tau3 is float noise). The only regimes without agreement are mathematically degenerate (rank-1 T: identical or exactly antipodal directions, or N=1), where neither side defines a pole and PMTools reports a noise-driven MAD while PmagPy clamps to 0; and the exactly-horizontal-pole boundary (inc == 0 within noise) where the hemisphere choice is undefined on both sides and the comparison must be as an axis. Plan row needs to name both oracles (doprinc for the axis, domean DE-BFP for the MAD) and the hemisphere adapter.

adapters_required: Inputs to PmagPy must be the values PMTools actually uses: polarity-reversed rows antipoded and all angles rounded to 0.1 deg (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:21-30); .dir inputs are already 0.1 deg so this is a no-op for them, not for CSV/XLSX with more decimals.

doprinc input: nested list [[dec, inc], ...] (2 columns -> unit vectors, pmag.py:2783-2790). domean input: rows [index, dec, inc, 1.0, '', 'g'], start=0, end=N-1, pass copy.deepcopy (domean mutates rows, pmag.py:2896), calculation_type 'DE-BFP'.

Hemisphere: PMTools pole has inc <= 0 (calculatePCA_dir.ts:56 reflects when z > 0); doprinc V3 has inc >= 0 (doflip pmag.py:6527); domean DE-BFP v3 sign is whatever numpy returns (pmag.py:3018). Adapter: antipode the oracle direction when its inc > 0; assert by angle between vectors, and as an axis (mod 180) when |inc| < ~1e-6 deg.

MAD: take domean DE-BFP 'specimen_mad' (clamps tau3 < 0 to 0, pmag.py:2974-2975) or compute atan(sqrt(t3/t2+t3/t1)) from doprinc tau with max(tau3, 0); PMTools maps a non-finite result to 0 (calculatePCA_dir.ts:63). Use tolerance ~1e-5 deg when N = 2 (tau3 is pure noise), 1e-9 otherwise.
Run the oracle twice per case: on (Dgeo, Igeo) and on (Dstrat, Istrat); PMTools returns both frames from one call.

Skip or treat as degenerate any case whose orientation matrix is rank 1 (N = 1, all directions identical, or all exactly antipodal): numpy returns complex eigenvalues (observed: (1+0j, -2.5e-17+2.1e-17j, ...)) and the pole is arbitrary on both sides. N = 1 is unreachable from the UI (InterpretationSetter.tsx:50 requires >= 2).

Avoid synthetic inputs with exactly equal eigenvalues: tauV picks the middle eigenvalue with `!=` (pmag.py:2686-2688), leaving t2 = 0 and ind2 = 1 on exact ties, which breaks the oracle's MAD (division by zero) while PMTools' indexOf-based sort still returns a value.
convention_differences: Pole hemisphere: PMTools upper (negative inclination; calculatePCA_dir.ts:56, same convention as the PCA page's plane fit calculatePCA_pmd.ts:55) vs doprinc lower (pmag.py:6512-6528 via doflip) vs domean DE-BFP unnormalised (pmag.py:3018).

Orientation-matrix scale: PMTools TMatrix divides each product by N (matrix.ts:65); pmag.Tmatrix does not (pmag.py:2713). Irrelevant after both sides divide the eigenvalues by the trace (eigManipulations.ts:7-20; pmag.py:2674-2677).

Centring: neither side centres for this fit (PMTools: centerMass declared at calculatePCA_dir.ts:24 but never subtracted; PmagPy: DE-BFP excluded from centring at pmag.py:2954-2960; doprinc never centres). The thesis matrix 1..3 (thesis.txt:331-345) is the centred covariance H, which applies to the PCA-page line fit, not to a great circle through the origin.

Negative tau3 noise: domean clamps to 0 (pmag.py:2974-2975); doprinc does not clamp (tau3 = -4e-17 observed at N=2); PMTools does not clamp but replaces a NaN/Infinity MAD by 0 (calculatePCA_dir.ts:63).

Input rounding: PMTools rounds inputs to 0.1 deg before fitting (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:27-30) and outputs to 0.1 deg in the tables (rawStatisticsDIRToInterpretation.ts:35-42); PmagPy rounds nothing.

Polarity flags: PMTools antipodes reversed rows first (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:23-26); the fit is invariant to this (T is sign-invariant), verified: sample.dir with rows 2,4,6,8 reversed gives the same pole to 1.7e-13 deg.

Declination at a vertical pole is arbitrary on both sides (PMTools 180, doprinc 0 for all-horizontal directions); tie-breaking of the hemisphere at an exactly horizontal pole depends on the eigensolver's sign noise on both sides (PMTools reflects only when z > 0, doprinc flips only when inc < 0).
Extra PmagPy outputs with no PMTools counterpart: V1/V2 directions, specimen_dang (angle centre-of-mass to pole); extra PMTools display with no PmagPy counterpart: Kgeo/Kstrat = 0.

final.thesis_agreement: Partly. The MAD formula in the code (calculatePCA_dir.ts:61-62, atan sqrt(lambda_min/lambda_int + lambda_min/lambda_max)) is exactly thesis formula (1..2) for planes (thesis.txt:325-329). The thesis defines the eigenvalues on the centred matrix H (formula 1..3, thesis.txt:331-345), but the DIR-page GC code uses the uncentred orientation matrix T = (1/N) sum x x^T (matrix.ts:56-71; centerMass at calculatePCA_dir.ts:24 is never applied). For a great circle, i.e. a plane through the origin of the unit sphere, the uncentred matrix is the correct one and it is what PmagPy uses for DE-BFP (pmag.py:2954-2960 skips centring for planes) and in doprinc (pmag.py:6505); the thesis's centred H describes the PCA-page line fit. The thesis describes the DIR-page GC as 'the intersection of remagnetisation circles' (thesis.txt:1011-1013) without a formula; the minimum eigenvector of the orientation matrix of the circles' poles is the least-squares common intersection point, so the code matches that wording. The thesis also lists a GCN method on the DIR page (thesis.txt:1013) that the app does not implement (only a hotkey that stores zeros). The results table description (thesis.txt:1049-1052: Dgeo/Igeo, Dstrat/Istrat, MAD or a95 and k) matches the columns shown. The hemisphere convention (pole reported with inclination <= 0) is not stated in the thesis: not verified against any text.
final.confidence_reason: Every claim rests on opened source lines (PMTools TypeScript and pmagpy 4.3.14 pmag.py/ipmag.py, version confirmed at version.py:7) and on runs of both implementations on identical inputs: 16 cases in two frames, with agreement at the 1e-13 deg level for the pole and <= 8e-13 deg for the MAD wherever the problem is non-degenerate, and eigenvalue parity at 2.8e-16. The UI click path for 'gc' and the 'gcn' hotkey were traced by reading (not by driving the browser); the 'gcn' zero result was reproduced by calling the dispatcher directly. The hemisphere convention has no thesis statement to check against.

mapping.pmtools_method: Inputs per site row: dec, inc (degrees, taken from Dgeo/Igeo or Dstrat/Istrat per the Reference selector, optionally reversed by the user's R selection via Direction.reversePolarity = (dec+180)%360, -inc, then ROUNDED to 1 decimal with toFixed(1) — VGPmodalContent.tsx:62-74), a95 = the DIR file's MAD column for that reference (interpretation.MADgeo|MADstrat, VGPmodalContent.tsx:75; for .pmm this is the a95g/a95s column, parserPMM.ts:24,32; for .dir it is cols 51-58, parserDIR.ts:35, which is PCA MAD when the file came from the PCA page; missing -> 0), site lat/lon in degrees, unrounded, from the Sites CSV/XLSX columns 'lat','lon' (parserCSV_SitesLatLon.ts:14-24) or the editable table (missing -> 0). Hidden rows are excluded before calculation (:52). calculateVGP.ts: paleolatitude lambda = atan(0.5 tan I) (Direction.ts:19, degrees); pole latitude phi_p = asin(sin(slat) sin(lambda) + cos(slat) cos(lambda) cos(dec)) (:25-29); longitude offset c = acos((sin(lambda) - sin(phi_p) sin(slat)) / (cos(slat) cos(phi_p))) in degrees (:30-34, argument NOT clamped to [-1,1]); pole longitude = slon + c, or slon - c when sin(dec) < 0 (:41-42); if < 0 add 360 (:44-46) — never reduced when > 360. dp = 2 a95 / (1 + 3 cos^2 I), dm = a95 cos(lambda) / cos(I) (:50-51), computed only when a95 is truthy (a95 = 0 or undefined -> dp/dm undefined; the UI turns that into 0, VGPmodalContent.tsx:78-79). No hemisphere flip: a reverse direction yields a southern pole as computed; the user's reverse selection is applied to the direction before the VGP (verified to give the antipodal pole). Pole longitude is reported in 0..360 (except the >360 defect). Returned {poleLatitude, poleLongitude, paleoLatitude, dp, dm}; table shows them at 1 decimal. Mean pole (VGP/Graphs.tsx:28-31): plain Fisher mean (calculateFisherMean.ts:21-94) of unit vectors built from (poleLongitude as declination, poleLatitude as inclination) over ALL rows of vgpData, no polarity flip, no weighting; outputs mean declination (=plon, 0..360), mean inclination (=plat), a95 = acos(1 - ((20^(1/(N-1)) - 1)(N-R)/R)) in degrees (180 if the argument is negative; key named MAD), k = (N-1)/(N-R) (Infinity when N == R), N, R, csd = 81/sqrt(k). VGPMean shows plat, plon, a95, k, N, R at 2 decimals; the copy string folds plon to -180..180. Deterministic, no iteration, no randomness, no constants beyond 20 (Fisher 95%), 0.5 (dipole), 81 (csd).

mapping.verdict_explanation: Three different things hide behind the row. (1) calculateVGP (live) is exact-with-adapter against pmag.dia_vgp for all regular inputs: 24 point cases plus the 9 exampleDIR.pmm directions agree on pole lon/lat to <= 4e-13 deg and on dp/dm to <= 9e-15 (the dp forms 2a95/(1+3cos^2 I) and a95(1+3cos^2 p)/2 are algebraically identical given tan I = 2 cot p), and paleoLatitude equals pmag.plat to 4e-15. But three edge families mismatch, all new: the acos argument at calculateVGP.ts:30-34 is not clamped, so for declination exactly 0/180/360 (which the UI's toFixed(1) produces) the pole longitude is NaN in 246 of 867 swept cases where PmagPy gives a finite value; longitude is never reduced below 360 (site lon 350 -> 494.69 vs 134.69); dm at exactly |I| = 90 is a95 instead of the analytic 2·a95. Degenerate inputs (site |lat| = 90, pole |lat| = 90) differ but are not comparable. (2) The mean pole (live) is exact-with-adapter against pmag.fisher_mean on [[plon, plat]] pairs: example mean agrees to 6e-14 on plon/plat/A95/k/N/R/csd; N = 2 bit-exact; N = 1 and antipodal pairs are not comparable (PmagPy returns only dec/inc for N < 2; PMTools shows a95 NaN, k Infinity). convention_differences: Pole longitude branch: PMTools uses sign of sin(dec) (calculateVGP.ts:42); PmagPy uses cos p > sin(slat) sin(plat) (pmag.py:1403) — same result whenever both are finite (verified on 33 point cases and 618 sweep cases)

PMTools computes the longitude offset with acos of a ratio (ill-conditioned and unclamped near ±1, calculateVGP.ts:30-34); PmagPy with asin of a clamped beta (pmag.py:1375, 1386-1401): this alone causes the NaN and the 1e-4 deg noise on the site meridian
Range normalisation: PMTools adds 360 only when negative (calculateVGP.ts:44-46); dia_vgp wraps both ways (1411-1423); vgp_calc uses % 360 (ipmag.py:3132-3133)

dp/dm written in inclination form (2a95/(1+3cos^2 I), a95 cos(lambda)/cos I) vs colatitude form (a95(1+3cos^2 p)/2, a95 sin p/cos I); analytically identical, numerically identical except at |I| = 90 where the PMTools degree round-trip of lambda loses the factor 2

Hemisphere: neither side flips poles; PMTools relies on the user reversing directions (R) before 'Calculate VGPs'; PmagPy offers _rev columns (vgp_calc) / anti=1 (scalc_vgp_df) / fisher_by_pol instead

The a95 feeding dp/dm is the DIR file's MAD column (MADgeo/MADstrat): alpha95 for .pmm (a95g/a95s), but PCA MAD when a .dir was produced from the PCA page; PmagPy assumes a true alpha95

Not verified: the NaN propagation into the on-screen mean pole and the 'NaN' strings in the table were reasoned from code, not executed in the browser; the paleomagnetism.org Site.poleFrom source cited in the in-code comment was not checked; the identical-poles edge (R = 3.0000000000000004) is platform float noise and may differ on CI.
mapping.thesis_agreement: The thesis has no formula for the VGP or the mean pole; it describes the module only at UI level. thesis.txt:1058-1092 (§2.3.1) and :1350-1395 (§3.4): sites file with columns lat, lon (age, plate_id optional) is required (:1081-1087, matches parserCSV_SitesLatLon.ts:14-18 and VGPmodalContent.tsx:141-163); the VGP table is exportable to .vgp/.gpml/.csv/.xlsx (:1074-1075, matches converters/vgp.ts); the stereogram uses pole latitude as inclination and longitude as declination (:1075-1077, matches dataToStereoVGP.ts:32-36); the mean direction is computed automatically by Fisher statistics (:1077-1078, matches VGP/Graphs.tsx:28-31). The published paper FZE0150.txt:355-359, 383 adds that the table shows dp/dm (95% confidence oval semi-axes) and paleolat, matching VGPDataTable.tsx:40-62. The code agrees with everything the thesis states; the pole formula itself is therefore specified only by the in-code comment citing paleomagnetism.org (calculateVGP.ts:11), which I did not verify against that source — PmagPy's dia_vgp is the only checked reference, and the fixtures README (src/__tests__/fixtures/vgp/README.md) already names Butler/Tauxe/dia_vgp as the citation targets.

final.pmtools_method: Inputs per site row: dec, inc (degrees, taken from Dgeo/Igeo or Dstrat/Istrat per the Reference selector, optionally reversed by the user's R selection via Direction.reversePolarity = (dec+180)%360, -inc, then ROUNDED to 1 decimal with toFixed(1) — VGPmodalContent.tsx:62-74), a95 = the DIR file's MAD column for that reference (interpretation.MADgeo|MADstrat, VGPmodalContent.tsx:75; for .pmm this is the a95g/a95s column, parserPMM.ts:24,32; for .dir it is cols 51-58, parserDIR.ts:35, which is PCA MAD when the file came from the PCA page; missing -> 0), site lat/lon in degrees, unrounded, from the Sites CSV/XLSX columns 'lat','lon' (parserCSV_SitesLatLon.ts:14-24) or the editable table (missing -> 0). Hidden rows are excluded before calculation (:52). calculateVGP.ts: paleolatitude lambda = atan(0.5 tan I) (Direction.ts:19, degrees); pole latitude phi_p = asin(sin(slat) sin(lambda) + cos(slat) cos(lambda) cos(dec)) (:25-29); longitude offset c = acos((sin(lambda) - sin(phi_p) sin(slat)) / (cos(slat) cos(phi_p))) in degrees (:30-34, argument NOT clamped to [-1,1]); pole longitude = slon + c, or slon - c when sin(dec) < 0 (:41-42); if < 0 add 360 (:44-46) — never reduced when > 360. dp = 2 a95 / (1 + 3 cos^2 I), dm = a95 cos(lambda) / cos(I) (:50-51), computed only when a95 is truthy (a95 = 0 or undefined -> dp/dm undefined; the UI turns that into 0, VGPmodalContent.tsx:78-79). No hemisphere flip: a reverse direction yields a southern pole as computed; the user's reverse selection is applied to the direction before the VGP (verified to give the antipodal pole). Pole longitude is reported in 0..360 (except the >360 defect). Returned {poleLatitude, poleLongitude, paleoLatitude, dp, dm}; table shows them at 1 decimal. Mean pole (VGP/Graphs.tsx:28-31): plain Fisher mean (calculateFisherMean.ts:21-94) of unit vectors built from (poleLongitude as declination, poleLatitude as inclination) over ALL rows of vgpData, no polarity flip, no weighting; outputs mean declination (=plon, 0..360), mean inclination (=plat), a95 = acos(1 - ((20^(1/(N-1)) - 1)(N-R)/R)) in degrees (180 if the argument is negative; key named MAD), k = (N-1)/(N-R) (Infinity when N == R), N, R, csd = 81/sqrt(k). VGPMean shows plat, plon, a95, k, N, R at 2 decimals; the copy string folds plon to -180..180. Deterministic, no iteration, no randomness, no constants beyond 20 (Fisher 95%), 0.5 (dipole), 81 (csd).
