final.verdict_explanation: Three different things hide behind the row. (1) calculateVGP (live) is exact-with-adapter against pmag.dia_vgp for all regular inputs: 24 point cases plus the 9 exampleDIR.pmm directions agree on pole lon/lat to <= 4e-13 deg and on dp/dm to <= 9e-15 (the dp forms 2a95/(1+3cos^2 I) and a95(1+3cos^2 p)/2 are algebraically identical given tan I = 2 cot p), and paleoLatitude equals pmag.plat to 4e-15. But three edge families mismatch, all new: the acos argument at calculateVGP.ts:30-34 is not clamped, so for declination exactly 0/180/360 (which the UI's toFixed(1) produces) the pole longitude is NaN in 246 of 867 swept cases where PmagPy gives a finite value; longitude is never reduced below 360 (site lon 350 -> 494.69 vs 134.69); dm at exactly |I| = 90 is a95 instead of the analytic 2·a95. Degenerate inputs (site |lat| = 90, pole |lat| = 90) differ but are not comparable. (2) The mean pole (live) is exact-with-adapter against pmag.fisher_mean on [[plon, plat]] pairs: example mean agrees to 6e-14 on plon/plat/A95/k/N/R/csd; N = 2 bit-exact; N = 1 and antipodal pairs are not comparable (PmagPy returns only dec/inc for N < 2; PMTools shows a95 NaN, k Infinity). (3) calculateButlerParameters, calculateBasicStatisticalParameters, Distribution and calculateCutoff are dead (only an unused import at dataToStereoDIR.ts:11; call removed in commit 8648630; live CUTOFF 45 works on directions at DIRPage/Graphs.tsx:61-88) and have no PmagPy equivalent; their outputs are unit-mixed (SCI-05/06, superseded by SCI-20). Note: src/__pb_scratch__/inventory exists and belongs to another agent; my PB-05-map folder was removed.

Compare longitudes modulo 360 (fold PMTools poleLongitude with % 360 only in the test's expected-mismatch branch; assert the raw >360 value as the recorded mismatch)

Mean pole: build [[poleLongitude, poleLatitude], ...] (lon in the dec slot, lat in the inc slot) for pmag.fisher_mean; map dec->plon, inc->plat, alpha95->MAD/a95, n->N, r->R; k 'inf' (string) -> Infinity; for N = 1 compare only dec/inc

Tolerance: 1e-9 abs on regular inputs (observed <= 4e-13); for dec exactly 0/180/360 either exclude the case, expect NaN (asserted mismatch), or allow 1e-4 deg on pole longitude (observed max 9.7e-5); exclude |plat| >= 89.999 and site |lat| = 90 as degenerate
Expect NaN/absent handling: PMTools NaN serializes as null in the fixture harness (computationFixtures.ts), so oracle JSON must encode NaN explicitly
convention_differences: Pole longitude branch: PMTools uses sign of sin(dec) (calculateVGP.ts:42); PmagPy uses cos p > sin(slat) sin(plat) (pmag.py:1403) — same result whenever both are finite (verified on 33 point cases and 618 sweep cases)

PMTools computes the longitude offset with acos of a ratio (ill-conditioned and unclamped near ±1, calculateVGP.ts:30-34); PmagPy with asin of a clamped beta (pmag.py:1375, 1386-1401): this alone causes the NaN and the 1e-4 deg noise on the site meridian
Range normalisation: PMTools adds 360 only when negative (calculateVGP.ts:44-46); dia_vgp wraps both ways (1411-1423); vgp_calc uses % 360 (ipmag.py:3132-3133)

dp/dm written in inclination form (2a95/(1+3cos^2 I), a95 cos(lambda)/cos I) vs colatitude form (a95(1+3cos^2 p)/2, a95 sin p/cos I); analytically identical, numerically identical except at |I| = 90 where the PMTools degree round-trip of lambda loses the factor 2

Hemisphere: neither side flips poles; PMTools relies on the user reversing directions (R) before 'Calculate VGPs'; PmagPy offers _rev columns (vgp_calc) / anti=1 (scalc_vgp_df) / fisher_by_pol instead
Mean pole labels: PMTools shows 'a95' (fisherMean key MAD) for what PmagPy's print_pole_mean calls A_95; PMTools also shows R, which PmagPy returns as 'r' but does not print
Mean pole of mixed polarity: both average without flipping (a95 = 180 for the mixed test); scientifically meaningless but consistent
The a95 feeding dp/dm is the DIR file's MAD column (MADgeo/MADstrat): alpha95 for .pmm (a95g/a95s), but PCA MAD when a .dir was produced from the PCA page; PmagPy assumes a true alpha95
Degenerate site at |lat| = 90: PMTools NaN; PmagPy returns a convention-dependent value (dia_vgp and vgp_calc even disagree for slat = -90: 40 vs 160)
Dead Butler path uses a fake site at (0, 0) and a radian confidence from Distribution.getConfidenceInterval (which is NaN because Distribution.R is never set, Distribution.ts:13)

final.confidence_reason: Every formula claim rests on lines I opened (calculateVGP.ts, Direction.ts, calculateFisherMean.ts, VGPmodalContent.tsx, VGP/Graphs.tsx, pmag.py 1329-1429 / 4431-4501 / 11586-11606, ipmag.py 165-208 / 2176-2208 / 3069-3172) and on 33 point cases, the 9-direction example, 7 mean-pole cases and an 867-case sweep that I ran on both sides from one shared cases.json; dead-code claims rest on grep of importers plus commit 8648630 and the live cutoff code at DIRPage/Graphs.tsx:61-88. Not verified: the NaN propagation into the on-screen mean pole and the 'NaN' strings in the table were reasoned from code, not executed in the browser; the paleomagnetism.org Site.poleFrom source cited in the in-code comment was not checked; the identical-poles edge (R = 3.0000000000000004) is platform float noise and may differ on CI.
final.thesis_agreement: The thesis has no formula for the VGP or the mean pole; it describes the module only at UI level. thesis.txt:1058-1092 (§2.3.1) and :1350-1395 (§3.4): sites file with columns lat, lon (age, plate_id optional) is required (:1081-1087, matches parserCSV_SitesLatLon.ts:14-18 and VGPmodalContent.tsx:141-163); the VGP table is exportable to .vgp/.gpml/.csv/.xlsx (:1074-1075, matches converters/vgp.ts); the stereogram uses pole latitude as inclination and longitude as declination (:1075-1077, matches dataToStereoVGP.ts:32-36); the mean direction is computed automatically by Fisher statistics (:1077-1078, matches VGP/Graphs.tsx:28-31). The published paper FZE0150.txt:355-359, 383 adds that the table shows dp/dm (95% confidence oval semi-axes) and paleolat, matching VGPDataTable.tsx:40-62. The code agrees with everything the thesis states; the pole formula itself is therefore specified only by the in-code comment citing paleomagnetism.org (calculateVGP.ts:11), which I did not verify against that source — PmagPy's dia_vgp is the only checked reference, and the fixtures README (src/__tests__/fixtures/vgp/README.md) already names Butler/Tauxe/dia_vgp as the citation targets.

mapping.pmtools_method: calculateMCFaddenIncMean(inclinations: number[]) -> {ginc, inc, n, r, k, a95, csd} | null. Inputs: inclinations in degrees, any sign. Preprocessing: |inc| taken for every value (:40, :63, :89), so polarity is discarded and all-negative data yields a positive mean (verified: case I equals case B bit-exactly). Empty array -> null (:41). N=1 -> gausspars returns null (:6) and the non-null assertion at :43 lets :47 throw TypeError (SCI-08). Step 1 (:43): Gaussian mean MI of |inc| and sample std (N-1). Step 2 (:47-59): if MI < 30 (strict) return {ginc: MI, inc: MI, n, r:0, k:0, a95:0, csd:0} (shallow branch). Step 3 (:61-66): colatitudes theta_i = (90-|inc_i|)*pi/180; SCOi = sum cos theta_i, SSOi = sum sin theta_i. Step 4 (:68-84): maximum-likelihood colatitude Oo found by a 1-D walk: start Oo = (90-MI) deg; eps(Oo) = N cos Oo + (sin^2 Oo - cos^2 Oo) SCOi - 2 sin Oo cos Oo SSOi; step Oo by -0.01 deg while MI>0 (+0.01 deg while MI<0); if |eps| grows, flip the sign of gaussparsRes.MI to reverse the walk (:82, this mutates the value later returned as ginc); stop at the first sign change of eps (:83), keeping the POST-crossing grid point. No iteration cap: inputs with eps(start)=0 exactly ([90,90,90], [30,30,30]) or with no zero crossing ([35,60,80], [31,45,60,75,89], [88,89,90,87]) oscillate forever (verified with a 3 s worker timeout). Step 5 (:86-100): S = sum sin(Oo - theta_i), C = sum cos(Oo - theta_i); k = (N-1)/(2(N-C)); inc = 90 - Oo (deg); r = 2C - N; a95 = acos(1 - 0.5 (S/C)^2 - f/(2 C k)) in degrees with f HARDCODED to 0 (:97, comment shows the intended fcalc(2, N-1)); csd = 81/sqrt(k). Constants: 30 deg shallow threshold, 0.01 deg step, 81 (csd). Deterministic, no randomness. Units: degrees in and out. No upper/lower confidence limits are computed.

pmagpy_oracles.method: McFadden & Reid (1982) inclination-only ML estimate: same misfit function as PMTools evaluated on a fixed grid Oo = 0..90 deg step 0.01; every sign change of the misfit is a candidate root (PRE-crossing grid index from np.diff), the root with the smallest second derivative U is chosen; then k, inc, r, alpha95 = acos(1 - 0.5 (S/C)^2 - f (N-C)/(C (N-1))) with f = fcalc(2, N-1) (algebraically identical to PMTools's commented f/(2 C k); checked numerically 0.006859275305211375 both), asymmetric limits after McElhinny & McFadden (2000). adapters_required: Input: none. Both take a plain array of inclinations in degrees; sign is irrelevant on both sides (abs). No declinations, no bedding, no coordinate frame.
Key rename: PMTools a95 <-> PmagPy alpha95; PMTools has no upper_confidence_limit / lower_confidence_limit.
Shallow branch (mean |inc| < 30): PmagPy omits the alpha95 key and prints a WARNING to stdout; the oracle generator must write alpha95 as 0 or null explicitly and must capture/discard stdout.
Numpy nan/inf (k, alpha95, csd for zero-scatter or N=1 inputs) must be serialised as null; PmagPy returns inc as numpy.float64 and r twice (fpars['r'] and a local R).
ginc: compare absolute values (PMTools's sign is an artefact of :82).
Tolerance: 0.02 deg on inc (0.01 deg grid, different origins and crossing sides), propagated to r/k/csd (use relative 1e-3 or compare at 2 significant digits past the grid effect); n bit-exact.

Input guard: the parity test must exclude inputs that hang PMTools (misfit exactly zero at the Gaussian guess, e.g. identical inclinations, or no zero crossing) because Jest cannot interrupt a synchronous infinite loop; the oracle generator must also catch IndexError from pmag.doincfish on no-root inputs (pmag.py:6291-6294) and TypeError from PMTools at N=1.
convention_differences: Polarity: both take |inc| (calculateMCFaddenIncMean.ts:40,63,89; pmag.py:6262-6264,6280), so the returned mean is always positive and all-negative data equals all-positive data (case I == case B on both sides).
Shallow rule: both use strict MI < 30 (:47; pmag.py:6270); an exact mean of 30 goes to the ML branch on both (case J2 agrees).

Root search: PmagPy scans a fixed 0..90 deg grid (step 0.01) and keeps the PRE-crossing grid point of the crossing with the smallest second derivative (pmag.py:6284-6299); PMTools walks a 0.01 deg grid anchored at 90-ginc from the Gaussian guess and keeps the POST-crossing point of the first crossing met (:68-84). Consequence: inc differs by < 0.02 deg; for inputs whose misfit has several roots the chosen root could differ (not observed in 18 cases, not verified).

Non-convergence: PmagPy prints 'No zeros found ...' and then crashes (IndexError at :6294); PMTools loops forever. PmagPy additionally returns a valid result for exact-root inputs where PMTools hangs ([90,90,90] -> inc 90, [30,30,30] -> inc 30.000000000000007).
a95: PmagPy adds the F(2,N-1) term (pmag.py:6307-6308); PMTools stubs f=0 (:97). The two algebraic forms f/(2Ck) and f(N-C)/(C(N-1)) are identical, so restoring fcalc would give parity.
Extra PmagPy outputs: asymmetric upper/lower limits (pmag.py:6310-6311) have no PMTools counterpart.
Return shape: PmagPy prints warnings to stdout and omits 'alpha95' in the shallow branch; PMTools is silent and always returns all seven keys (or null for an empty array, or throws for N=1).
ginc: PmagPy's is always the positive Gaussian mean; PMTools's carries the sign left by the direction-reversal flag mutation (:82).

final.pmtools_method: calculateMCFaddenIncMean(inclinations: number[]) -> {ginc, inc, n, r, k, a95, csd} | null. Inputs: inclinations in degrees, any sign. Preprocessing: |inc| taken for every value (:40, :63, :89), so polarity is discarded and all-negative data yields a positive mean (verified: case I equals case B bit-exactly). Empty array -> null (:41). N=1 -> gausspars returns null (:6) and the non-null assertion at :43 lets :47 throw TypeError (SCI-08). Step 1 (:43): Gaussian mean MI of |inc| and sample std (N-1). Step 2 (:47-59): if MI < 30 (strict) return {ginc: MI, inc: MI, n, r:0, k:0, a95:0, csd:0} (shallow branch). Step 3 (:61-66): colatitudes theta_i = (90-|inc_i|)*pi/180; SCOi = sum cos theta_i, SSOi = sum sin theta_i. Step 4 (:68-84): maximum-likelihood colatitude Oo found by a 1-D walk: start Oo = (90-MI) deg; eps(Oo) = N cos Oo + (sin^2 Oo - cos^2 Oo) SCOi - 2 sin Oo cos Oo SSOi; step Oo by -0.01 deg while MI>0 (+0.01 deg while MI<0); if |eps| grows, flip the sign of gaussparsRes.MI to reverse the walk (:82, this mutates the value later returned as ginc); stop at the first sign change of eps (:83), keeping the POST-crossing grid point. No iteration cap: inputs with eps(start)=0 exactly ([90,90,90], [30,30,30]) or with no zero crossing ([35,60,80], [31,45,60,75,89], [88,89,90,87]) oscillate forever (verified with a 3 s worker timeout). Step 5 (:86-100): S = sum sin(Oo - theta_i), C = sum cos(Oo - theta_i); k = (N-1)/(2(N-C)); inc = 90 - Oo (deg); r = 2C - N; a95 = acos(1 - 0.5 (S/C)^2 - f/(2 C k)) in degrees with f HARDCODED to 0 (:97, comment shows the intended fcalc(2, N-1)); csd = 81/sqrt(k). Constants: 30 deg shallow threshold, 0.01 deg step, 81 (csd). Deterministic, no randomness. Units: degrees in and out. No upper/lower confidence limits are computed.

final.verdict_explanation: calculateMCFaddenIncMean is unreachable from the UI: the DIR page offers only fisher / mcFad / gc (types.ts:10, ToolsDIR.tsx:218-220, calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:45-47), the PCA page only pca / pca0 / gc / gcn (types.ts:8, ToolsPMD.tsx:202-205), hotkeys list only Fisher and McFadden (GlobalHooks.ts:293,302), no locale string mentions an inclination-only mode, the only importer is its own Part A test, and git history (02fbf64 -> 06d1b94 -> e3a6b67) shows it was never wired in. The thesis does not describe the method at all (thesis.txt:295-373 covers Bingham/PCA/Fisher/McFadden-1988 only; the DIR-page method list at thesis.txt:1009-1013 is FISHER, MCFADDEN, GC, GCN; FZE0150.txt:219 lists Fisher, McFadden, GreatCircle), and ledger SCI-20 already has Ivan's approval to delete it. Independently of liveness, pmag.doincfish IS the right oracle if the function is ever kept: same McFadden & Reid misfit function, same k, r, csd formulas, same 30 deg shallow rule, same abs() polarity handling, and the ML inclination agrees within the 0.01 deg grid (max observed 0.01 deg, bound < 0.02 deg; bit-level agreement 6e-14 when the grids coincide, case A). Known mismatches: a95 (SCI-07, PMTools stubs the F-term; its a95 equals PmagPy's f=0 reconstruction to 1e-16), N=1 throws (SCI-08), plus two uncatalogued defects found here: ginc comes back sign-flipped whenever the walk reverses (A, D, E) and the search never terminates for exact-root or no-root inputs (5 of 18 cases). PmagPy's own no-zero fallback raises IndexError in 4.3.14, so even the oracle cannot cover steep/no-root inputs. adapters_required: Input: none. Both take a plain array of inclinations in degrees; sign is irrelevant on both sides (abs). No declinations, no bedding, no coordinate frame.
Key rename: PMTools a95 <-> PmagPy alpha95; PMTools has no upper_confidence_limit / lower_confidence_limit.
Shallow branch (mean |inc| < 30): PmagPy omits the alpha95 key and prints a WARNING to stdout; the oracle generator must write alpha95 as 0 or null explicitly and must capture/discard stdout.
Numpy nan/inf (k, alpha95, csd for zero-scatter or N=1 inputs) must be serialised as null; PmagPy returns inc as numpy.float64 and r twice (fpars['r'] and a local R).
ginc: compare absolute values (PMTools's sign is an artefact of :82).
Tolerance: 0.02 deg on inc (0.01 deg grid, different origins and crossing sides), propagated to r/k/csd (use relative 1e-3 or compare at 2 significant digits past the grid effect); n bit-exact.

Input guard: the parity test must exclude inputs that hang PMTools (misfit exactly zero at the Gaussian guess, e.g. identical inclinations, or no zero crossing) because Jest cannot interrupt a synchronous infinite loop; the oracle generator must also catch IndexError from pmag.doincfish on no-root inputs (pmag.py:6291-6294) and TypeError from PMTools at N=1.
convention_differences: Polarity: both take |inc| (calculateMCFaddenIncMean.ts:40,63,89; pmag.py:6262-6264,6280), so the returned mean is always positive and all-negative data equals all-positive data (case I == case B on both sides).
Shallow rule: both use strict MI < 30 (:47; pmag.py:6270); an exact mean of 30 goes to the ML branch on both (case J2 agrees).

Root search: PmagPy scans a fixed 0..90 deg grid (step 0.01) and keeps the PRE-crossing grid point of the crossing with the smallest second derivative (pmag.py:6284-6299); PMTools walks a 0.01 deg grid anchored at 90-ginc from the Gaussian guess and keeps the POST-crossing point of the first crossing met (:68-84). Consequence: inc differs by < 0.02 deg; for inputs whose misfit has several roots the chosen root could differ (not observed in 18 cases, not verified).

Non-convergence: PmagPy prints 'No zeros found ...' and then crashes (IndexError at :6294); PMTools loops forever. PmagPy additionally returns a valid result for exact-root inputs where PMTools hangs ([90,90,90] -> inc 90, [30,30,30] -> inc 30.000000000000007).
a95: PmagPy adds the F(2,N-1) term (pmag.py:6307-6308); PMTools stubs f=0 (:97). The two algebraic forms f/(2Ck) and f(N-C)/(C(N-1)) are identical, so restoring fcalc would give parity.
Extra PmagPy outputs: asymmetric upper/lower limits (pmag.py:6310-6311) have no PMTools counterpart.
Return shape: PmagPy prints warnings to stdout and omits 'alpha95' in the shallow branch; PMTools is silent and always returns all seven keys (or null for an empty array, or throws for N=1).
ginc: PmagPy's is always the positive Gaussian mean; PMTools's carries the sign left by the direction-reversal flag mutation (:82).

final.confidence_reason: Liveness rests on three independent checks that all agree (importer grep, git log -S over every commit that touched the symbol, and the enumerated UI mode unions/buttons/hotkeys/locales), plus SCI-20 and the thesis method list. The numeric comparison ran both implementations on the same 18 input sets (two real files, the existing fixtures, the PmagPy docstring example and edge cases); the real-source Jest numbers match the compiled-copy numbers bit-for-bit, and every PmagPy figure is from pmag.doincfish 4.3.14 with its stdout captured. Each formula claim cites the line on both sides, and the F-term equivalence was checked numerically. Not verified: the original McFadden & Reid (1982) equations (paper unavailable; two academic-search lookups returned 0 results), the PmagPy command-line program incfish.py (not installed), and whether multi-root inputs can make the two implementations select different roots (not observed in any case).
final.thesis_agreement: The thesis does not describe an inclination-only mean anywhere. Section 1.3 (thesis.txt:295-373) covers only Bingham/PCA (eq. 1.1-1.3), the Fisher distribution (eq. 1.4-1.5, lines 348-358) and the McFadden 1988 combined-circles modification (lines 366-370). The DIR-page method list (thesis.txt:1009-1013) is FISHER, MCFADDEN, GC, GCN, and the published paper lists 'Fisher, McFadden, GreatCircle' (FZE0150.txt:219). Grep for 'Reid', 'inclination-only' / 'только по наклон' and '1982' finds only the Khramov 1982 reference (thesis.txt:351, 1509). So there is no thesis specification for calculateMCFaddenIncMean to agree or disagree with; the function sits outside the thesis, which is consistent with it never having been wired into the UI.

mapping.pmtools_method: Inputs: the selected DIR rows (>= 2, enforced by InterpretationSetter.tsx:50). Dispatcher preprocessing (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:17-37): rows whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs get reversePolarity (D+180 mod 360, -I; applied to GC rows too, harmless because the algorithm is invariant to the pole sign), then Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat are rounded to 0.1 deg (toFixed(1)). Plane marker: row.gcNormal (GlobalTypes.ts:67), set by the .dir/.csv/.xlsx/.mdir parsers when the CODE column starts with uppercase 'GC'; the stored D/I of such a row is the pole (normal) to the great circle (thesis.txt:1010-1012: 'normals to remagnetization circles'; PCA-page GC fits store the v3 eigenvector reflected to z<=0, calculatePCA_pmd.ts:51,55). Degrees in, degrees out; Cartesian x=cos D cos I, y=sin D cos I, z=sin I (Direction.ts:29-39), same as pmag.dir2cart. Per frame (geographic, stratigraphic) mcFaddenCombineMean(gcNormals, directions): M = number of lines, N = number of circles. For each circle, in input order (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:62-89): build 194 points on the great circle (getRawPlaneData -> createConfidenceEllipse(90,90,194): psi_i = i*pi/96.5, x=cos psi, y=sin psi, z=0, rotated to the pole; spacing 1.865 deg; point 0 and 193 coincide), and pick the grid point that maximises |sum of lines + already chosen circle points + this point| (strict '>' from 0, so index 0 wins ties unless rounding noise). Each circle is visited exactly once (no re-visit, no iteration, order-dependent). Final: R = |sum of lines + chosen points| (:95-104), mean = that vector / R -> atan2/asin (:107-108; declination in [0,360], can return exactly 360). k = (2M+N-2)/(2(M+N-R)) (:110) = (Q-1)/(M+N-R) with Q = M+N/2 (:113). csd = 81/sqrt(k) (:111). a95: b = (1/0.05)^(1/(Q-1)) - 1; a = 1-((Q-1)/(kR))*b; a<-1 -> -1; a95 = acos(a) in deg; a<0 -> 180 (:114-118). No Q clamp, no seed for M=0, no NaN guards. Returns {direction, MAD: a95, k, R, N: M+N, csd} (:129-136). With N=0 circles the loop is skipped and the formulas reduce exactly to Fisher (verified bit-exact against the FISHER mode and pmag.fisher_mean). Deterministic, no randomness. Constants: 0.05 (p), 81 (csd), 194 grid points.

pmagpy_oracles.input_format: list of dicts with 'dec','inc' (2.5) or 'dir_dec','dir_inc' (3.0, detected by 'dir_dec' in data[0], :4886); a record is a plane iff rec[direction_type_key] == 'p' exactly (lowercase, :5050; 'P' counts as a line, verified); if the key is absent, falls back to method codes containing 'DE-BFP' (:5059-5071); else everything is a line (:5072-5079). Tilt key optional (:4890-4893). Values may be numbers or numeric strings (float() at :5047).
pmagpy_oracles.outputs: Strings with trailing space: dec '%7.1f ', inc '%7.1f ', R '%5.4f ', K '%6.0f ' or 'inf', alpha95 '%7.1f ', n_total/n_lines/n_planes '%i ', tilt_correction (:4948-4961). No csd. Returned, not printed (prints only for empty data per docstring; data=[] actually raises IndexError at :4886, not tested).
pmagpy_oracles.method: McFadden & McElhinny 1988. n_planes>0: seed V = E/|E| (E = sum of line unit vectors) or dir2cart(180,-45) when no lines (:4904-4913); calculate_best_fit_vectors (:4976-5018): initial points vclose(pole,V) (:4992-4995), then sweeps: for each plane remove its point from U, V=U/|U|, new point = vclose(pole,V), movement = acos(new.old) deg; stop when the max movement in a sweep is <= 0.1 deg (:4998-5016). vclose (:4963-4973): lam=V.L, X=(V-lam L)/sqrt(1-lam^2), NaN when lam=+-1. Final U = E + sum(XV), R=|U|, dec/inc = cart2dir(U/R) (:4916-4923). NP = n_lines + 0.5 n_planes clamped to >= 1.1 (:4926-4928); K=(NP-1)/(n_total-R); fac=(20^(1/(NP-1))-1)(NP-1)/K; a=1-fac/R; |a|>1 -> 1; a<0 -> -a; a95=arccos(a) deg (:4930-4939); n_total==R -> a95=0, K='inf' (:4940-4942). n_planes==0: fisher_mean(fdata) (:4943-4946); a lone line then raises KeyError('n') (verified).

mapping.verdict_explanation: pmag.dolnp is the correct oracle for this row (same MM88 model: poles to planes, N' = n_lines + n_planes/2, identical k and a95 algebra), but PMTools today gives different numbers on every input that contains a great circle: it chooses each circle's point once, greedily, on a 194-point grid, while dolnp iterates the closed-form closest point to convergence. Measured gaps: 0.04-0.39 deg on the locked fixture (stratigraphic I 25.40 vs 25.04, order-dependent by 0.745 deg in PMTools), 0.05 deg on a real Kola file (table shows D 348.6 vs dolnp 348.4), 0.19 deg for 1 line + 1 circle, 1.2 deg for 1 line + 4 circles, and arbitrary results for circles only. That is ledger item SCI-23 (blocked). Three branches differ by convention regardless of SCI-23: a<0 gives a95 = 180 in PMTools vs arccos(-a) in dolnp (43.9 deg on the constructed case), dolnp clamps N' to 1.1 and seeds circles-only input at 180/-45 while PMTools does neither, and N=1 inputs (unreachable from the UI) make dolnp raise or return NaN. The directions-only path (no gcNormal rows) is bit-exact against dolnp's fisher_mean branch and against PMTools' own FISHER mode. Two new input-side findings: .pmm import never sets gcNormal, and PMTools' own PCA-page plane fits export CODE 'gc'/'gcn' in lowercase, which the parsers do not recognise, so MCFAD treats both as lines.

adapters_required: Row -> record per frame: {'dec': Dgeo|Dstrat, 'inc': Igeo|Istrat, 'dir_type': 'p' if row.gcNormal else 'l'}; call pmag.dolnp(records, 'dir_type') once for geographic and once for stratigraphic (the value must be exactly lowercase 'p'; any other value is a line).

Reproduce the dispatcher preprocessing first when testing the live path: reversePolarity for reversed ids and toFixed(1) rounding of D/I (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:24-31); fixture inputs are already at 0.1 deg so the raw function and the dispatcher give identical numbers (verified on the Kola file).
Parse dolnp output: .strip() then float(); K may be the string 'inf'; dec/inc/alpha95 are at 0.1 deg, R at 1e-4, K at integer precision.

For full precision use the replica: pmag.process_data_for_mean + seed V (E/|E| or dir2cart(180,-45,1)) + pmag.calculate_best_fit_vectors + pmag.cart2dir and the formulas of pmag.py:4925-4942 (verified to reproduce dolnp's strings on 32 blocks); keep it as a scripts/gen_mcfadden.py generator in the style of scripts/gen_fisher.py.
Field renames: alpha95 -> MAD, K -> k, n_total -> N, R -> R, dec/inc -> direction; csd = 81/sqrt(K).
No pole-sign adapter: both sides are invariant to flipping a gcNormal row (dolnp pole flipped: identical; PMTools reversed GC row: identical to 1e-8).

Exclude from parity: N<2 rows (UI never sends them; dolnp raises KeyError for one line, returns all-NaN for one circle), circles-only selections (dolnp seeds 180/-45 and clamps NP to 1.1), exactly antipodal line sets and lines parallel to a pole (dolnp NaN via vclose beta=0).
Measure agreement with a chord or clamped dot product, not pmag.angle (NaN for identical directions).
convention_differences: Plane marker: PMTools boolean gcNormal derived from CODE starting with uppercase 'GC' (parserDIR.ts:108 etc.); dolnp uses direction_type == 'p' or method code 'DE-BFP'.

Search for the point on each circle: PMTools single greedy pass over a 194-point grid in row order (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:62-89); dolnp closed-form closest point iterated until max movement <= 0.1 deg (pmag.py:4998-5016). Both are order-dependent at full precision (PMTools 0.745 deg, dolnp 0.009 deg on the fixture); a tight iteration is order-invariant to 1e-13.
Seed for circles-only input: dolnp dec 180 / inc -45 (pmag.py:4906-4908); PMTools none (winner decided by rounding noise of the grid norm).
N' clamp: dolnp NP = max(n_lines + 0.5 n_planes, 1.1) (pmag.py:4927-4928); PMTools Q = M + N/2 unclamped (k = 0 / NaN, a95 NaN, csd Infinity for M=0, N=2; k = -Infinity, a95 0 for M=0, N=1).
a < 0 branch: PMTools a95 = 180 (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:118, same as pmag.fisher_mean:4499-4500); dolnp a95 = arccos(-a) for -1 < a < 0 and 180 only when a <= -1 (pmag.py:4936-4939).
n_total == R: dolnp a95 = 0, K = 'inf' (pmag.py:4940-4942); PMTools k = Infinity or NaN (0/0 when 2M+N-2 == 0).
Output precision: PMTools floats; dolnp strings at 0.1 deg / 1e-4 / integer K; dolnp has no csd.
Field naming: PMTools 'MAD' holds a95 and the UI column is labelled MADgeo/MADstrat; dolnp 'alpha95'.
Preprocessing: PMTools rounds inputs to 0.1 deg and applies reversePolarity to reversed ids before the mean; dolnp takes records as given.
Declination of a mean exactly at D = 0 can print as 360.0 on both sides (PMTools atan2 path, dolnp arctan2 % 360 of a negative tiny y).

mapping.thesis_agreement: Partial. thesis.txt:366-370 says that for a mixed set of directions and remagnetization circles the Fisher statistics are replaced by the McFadden (1988) modification in which 'iteratively' a direction is sought along each circle that maximises the length of the mean vector; the code maximises R (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:72-82) but does it in one greedy pass per circle on a 194-point grid with no iteration (:62-89), so the 'iteratively' part is not implemented (known SCI-23; THESIS_FORMULAS.md:148-152 also says iterative and gives no formula or stop rule). thesis.txt:1010-1012 describes the MCFADDEN button as the modified Fisher statistics for data 'represented as normals to remagnetization circles', which matches the gcNormal flag and the pole-to-plane representation used by both PMTools and dolnp. The thesis gives no k/a95 formulas for the mixed case; PMTools' k and a95 (lines 110-118) match the MM88 formulas as implemented in pmag.dolnp:4925-4939 (Q = M + N/2 = NP) except for the N' clamp and the a<0 branch. thesis.txt:1549-1550 cites McFadden and McElhinny 1988 (ref 14); the paper text itself was not available and is not verified.

final.pmtools_method: Inputs: the selected DIR rows (>= 2, enforced by InterpretationSetter.tsx:50). Dispatcher preprocessing (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:17-37): rows whose id is in reversedDirectionsIDs get reversePolarity (D+180 mod 360, -I; applied to GC rows too, harmless because the algorithm is invariant to the pole sign), then Dgeo/Igeo/Dstrat/Istrat are rounded to 0.1 deg (toFixed(1)). Plane marker: row.gcNormal (GlobalTypes.ts:67), set by the .dir/.csv/.xlsx/.mdir parsers when the CODE column starts with uppercase 'GC'; the stored D/I of such a row is the pole (normal) to the great circle (thesis.txt:1010-1012: 'normals to remagnetization circles'; PCA-page GC fits store the v3 eigenvector reflected to z<=0, calculatePCA_pmd.ts:51,55). Degrees in, degrees out; Cartesian x=cos D cos I, y=sin D cos I, z=sin I (Direction.ts:29-39), same as pmag.dir2cart. Per frame (geographic, stratigraphic) mcFaddenCombineMean(gcNormals, directions): M = number of lines, N = number of circles. For each circle, in input order (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:62-89): build 194 points on the great circle (getRawPlaneData -> createConfidenceEllipse(90,90,194): psi_i = i*pi/96.5, x=cos psi, y=sin psi, z=0, rotated to the pole; spacing 1.865 deg; point 0 and 193 coincide), and pick the grid point that maximises |sum of lines + already chosen circle points + this point| (strict '>' from 0, so index 0 wins ties unless rounding noise). Each circle is visited exactly once (no re-visit, no iteration, order-dependent). Final: R = |sum of lines + chosen points| (:95-104), mean = that vector / R -> atan2/asin (:107-108; declination in [0,360], can return exactly 360). k = (2M+N-2)/(2(M+N-R)) (:110) = (Q-1)/(M+N-R) with Q = M+N/2 (:113). csd = 81/sqrt(k) (:111). a95: b = (1/0.05)^(1/(Q-1)) - 1; a = 1-((Q-1)/(kR))*b; a<-1 -> -1; a95 = acos(a) in deg; a<0 -> 180 (:114-118). No Q clamp, no seed for M=0, no NaN guards. Returns {direction, MAD: a95, k, R, N: M+N, csd} (:129-136). With N=0 circles the loop is skipped and the formulas reduce exactly to Fisher (verified bit-exact against the FISHER mode and pmag.fisher_mean). Deterministic, no randomness. Constants: 0.05 (p), 81 (csd), 194 grid points.

pmagpy_oracles.input_format: list of dicts with 'dec','inc' (2.5) or 'dir_dec','dir_inc' (3.0, detected by 'dir_dec' in data[0], :4886); a record is a plane iff rec[direction_type_key] == 'p' exactly (lowercase, :5050; 'P' counts as a line, verified); if the key is absent, falls back to method codes containing 'DE-BFP' (:5059-5071); else everything is a line (:5072-5079). Tilt key optional (:4890-4893). Values may be numbers or numeric strings (float() at :5047).
pmagpy_oracles.outputs: Strings with trailing space: dec '%7.1f ', inc '%7.1f ', R '%5.4f ', K '%6.0f ' or 'inf', alpha95 '%7.1f ', n_total/n_lines/n_planes '%i ', tilt_correction (:4948-4961). No csd. Returned, not printed (prints only for empty data per docstring; data=[] actually raises IndexError at :4886, not tested).
pmagpy_oracles.method: McFadden & McElhinny 1988. n_planes>0: seed V = E/|E| (E = sum of line unit vectors) or dir2cart(180,-45) when no lines (:4904-4913); calculate_best_fit_vectors (:4976-5018): initial points vclose(pole,V) (:4992-4995), then sweeps: for each plane remove its point from U, V=U/|U|, new point = vclose(pole,V), movement = acos(new.old) deg; stop when the max movement in a sweep is <= 0.1 deg (:4998-5016). vclose (:4963-4973): lam=V.L, X=(V-lam L)/sqrt(1-lam^2), NaN when lam=+-1. Final U = E + sum(XV), R=|U|, dec/inc = cart2dir(U/R) (:4916-4923). NP = n_lines + 0.5 n_planes clamped to >= 1.1 (:4926-4928); K=(NP-1)/(n_total-R); fac=(20^(1/(NP-1))-1)(NP-1)/K; a=1-fac/R; |a|>1 -> 1; a<0 -> -a; a95=arccos(a) deg (:4930-4939); n_total==R -> a95=0, K='inf' (:4940-4942). n_planes==0: fisher_mean(fdata) (:4943-4946); a lone line then raises KeyError('n') (verified).

final.verdict_explanation: pmag.dolnp is the correct oracle for this row (same MM88 model: poles to planes, N' = n_lines + n_planes/2, identical k and a95 algebra), but PMTools today gives different numbers on every input that contains a great circle: it chooses each circle's point once, greedily, on a 194-point grid, while dolnp iterates the closed-form closest point to convergence. Measured gaps: 0.04-0.39 deg on the locked fixture (stratigraphic I 25.40 vs 25.04, order-dependent by 0.745 deg in PMTools), 0.05 deg on a real Kola file (table shows D 348.6 vs dolnp 348.4), 0.19 deg for 1 line + 1 circle, 1.2 deg for 1 line + 4 circles, and arbitrary results for circles only. That is ledger item SCI-23 (blocked). Three branches differ by convention regardless of SCI-23: a<0 gives a95 = 180 in PMTools vs arccos(-a) in dolnp (43.9 deg on the constructed case), dolnp clamps N' to 1.1 and seeds circles-only input at 180/-45 while PMTools does neither, and N=1 inputs (unreachable from the UI) make dolnp raise or return NaN. The directions-only path (no gcNormal rows) is bit-exact against dolnp's fisher_mean branch and against PMTools' own FISHER mode. Two new input-side findings: .pmm import never sets gcNormal, and PMTools' own PCA-page plane fits export CODE 'gc'/'gcn' in lowercase, which the parsers do not recognise, so MCFAD treats both as lines.

adapters_required: Row -> record per frame: {'dec': Dgeo|Dstrat, 'inc': Igeo|Istrat, 'dir_type': 'p' if row.gcNormal else 'l'}; call pmag.dolnp(records, 'dir_type') once for geographic and once for stratigraphic (the value must be exactly lowercase 'p'; any other value is a line).

Reproduce the dispatcher preprocessing first when testing the live path: reversePolarity for reversed ids and toFixed(1) rounding of D/I (calculateStatisticsDIR.ts:24-31); fixture inputs are already at 0.1 deg so the raw function and the dispatcher give identical numbers (verified on the Kola file).
Parse dolnp output: .strip() then float(); K may be the string 'inf'; dec/inc/alpha95 are at 0.1 deg, R at 1e-4, K at integer precision.

For full precision use the replica: pmag.process_data_for_mean + seed V (E/|E| or dir2cart(180,-45,1)) + pmag.calculate_best_fit_vectors + pmag.cart2dir and the formulas of pmag.py:4925-4942 (verified to reproduce dolnp's strings on 32 blocks); keep it as a scripts/gen_mcfadden.py generator in the style of scripts/gen_fisher.py.
Field renames: alpha95 -> MAD, K -> k, n_total -> N, R -> R, dec/inc -> direction; csd = 81/sqrt(K).
No pole-sign adapter: both sides are invariant to flipping a gcNormal row (dolnp pole flipped: identical; PMTools reversed GC row: identical to 1e-8).

Exclude from parity: N<2 rows (UI never sends them; dolnp raises KeyError for one line, returns all-NaN for one circle), circles-only selections (dolnp seeds 180/-45 and clamps NP to 1.1), exactly antipodal line sets and lines parallel to a pole (dolnp NaN via vclose beta=0).
Measure agreement with a chord or clamped dot product, not pmag.angle (NaN for identical directions).
convention_differences: Plane marker: PMTools boolean gcNormal derived from CODE starting with uppercase 'GC' (parserDIR.ts:108 etc.); dolnp uses direction_type == 'p' or method code 'DE-BFP'.

Search for the point on each circle: PMTools single greedy pass over a 194-point grid in row order (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:62-89); dolnp closed-form closest point iterated until max movement <= 0.1 deg (pmag.py:4998-5016). Both are order-dependent at full precision (PMTools 0.745 deg, dolnp 0.009 deg on the fixture); a tight iteration is order-invariant to 1e-13.
Seed for circles-only input: dolnp dec 180 / inc -45 (pmag.py:4906-4908); PMTools none (winner decided by rounding noise of the grid norm).
N' clamp: dolnp NP = max(n_lines + 0.5 n_planes, 1.1) (pmag.py:4927-4928); PMTools Q = M + N/2 unclamped (k = 0 / NaN, a95 NaN, csd Infinity for M=0, N=2; k = -Infinity, a95 0 for M=0, N=1).
a < 0 branch: PMTools a95 = 180 (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:118, same as pmag.fisher_mean:4499-4500); dolnp a95 = arccos(-a) for -1 < a < 0 and 180 only when a <= -1 (pmag.py:4936-4939).
n_total == R: dolnp a95 = 0, K = 'inf' (pmag.py:4940-4942); PMTools k = Infinity or NaN (0/0 when 2M+N-2 == 0).
Output precision: PMTools floats; dolnp strings at 0.1 deg / 1e-4 / integer K; dolnp has no csd.
Field naming: PMTools 'MAD' holds a95 and the UI column is labelled MADgeo/MADstrat; dolnp 'alpha95'.
Preprocessing: PMTools rounds inputs to 0.1 deg and applies reversePolarity to reversed ids before the mean; dolnp takes records as given.
Declination of a mean exactly at D = 0 can print as 360.0 on both sides (PMTools atan2 path, dolnp arctan2 % 360 of a negative tiny y).

Not verified: the MM88 paper text (thesis and PmagPy agree on the model), browser behaviour of the PCA->DIR export round trip (verified at parser/converter level only), Linux CI float bits, and the pmag.circ vs getRawPlaneData comparison (proposed row PB-07e, not run).
final.thesis_agreement: Partial. thesis.txt:366-370 says that for a mixed set of directions and remagnetization circles the Fisher statistics are replaced by the McFadden (1988) modification in which 'iteratively' a direction is sought along each circle that maximises the length of the mean vector; the code maximises R (calculateMcFaddenCombineMean.ts:72-82) but does it in one greedy pass per circle on a 194-point grid with no iteration (:62-89), so the 'iteratively' part is not implemented (known SCI-23; THESIS_FORMULAS.md:148-152 also says iterative and gives no formula or stop rule). thesis.txt:1010-1012 describes the MCFADDEN button as the modified Fisher statistics for data 'represented as normals to remagnetization circles', which matches the gcNormal flag and the pole-to-plane representation used by both PMTools and dolnp. The thesis gives no k/a95 formulas for the mixed case; PMTools' k and a95 (lines 110-118) match the MM88 formulas as implemented in pmag.dolnp:4925-4939 (Q = M + N/2 = NP) except for the N' clamp and the a<0 branch. thesis.txt:1549-1550 cites McFadden and McElhinny 1988 (ref 14); the paper text itself was not available and is not verified.
